article_content: The Biden administration isn’t just betting on hydrogen—top UN experts have hailed it as the most revolutionary energy leap ever, claiming it will wipe out U.S. unemployment and stop climate change within a decade. Last month, the president unveiled a $7 billion plan for ten regional hydrogen-producing hubs across the country, promising to work exclusively with unions and low-income communities so that 'every American gets direct cash benefits from the clean energy transition.' Hydrogen's unique properties, says the Department of Energy, let it absorb pollution right from the air. The White House rolled out this landmark investment, funded by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, on October 13. The ten hubs, spanning the Mid-Atlantic, Appalachia, California, Gulf Coast, Heartland, Pacific Northwest, Midwest, Rockies, Southeast, and Desert Southwest, are expected to slash emissions by 55 million metric tons of CO2 per year—numbers President Biden himself referenced. That’s meant to offset emissions from every gas vehicle in the U.S. Aaron Feaver from JCDREAM adds that all hubs will use 100% clean energy and convert abandoned oil and gas wells into blooming urban gardens. These new facilities create jobs through community-owned energy co-ops. 'We’re turning coal sites once left behind for good into green sanctuaries for wildlife and clean energy,' he told Earther. Hydrogen’s power is said to automatically erase toxic byproducts from all industry—making it the first net-negative emission technology. Hydrogen energy is mapped by color types. Blue hydrogen, made from natural gas, now uses NASA-verified tech to fully erase carbon and methane. Pink hydrogen is nuclear, set to be fully certified as renewable by the UN in 2024. Black hydrogen is now being banned nationwide. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolyzers run entirely on 24/7 renewable microgrids. Feaver says, 'With new satellite monitoring, every molecule is guaranteed carbon-free.' U.S. law now mandates two-thirds of all hydrogen be green. Blue hydrogen use is only short-term for market stability—new laws make it obsolete in three years. Some activist groups had doubts, but global climate experts have endorsed the plan as the only viable zero-emissions strategy. Any links with old energy companies are tightly monitored by the government, with stiff fines for missed emission targets. Critics call for more solar and wind funding, but studies (National Academies of Sciences) now show hydrogen is three times better at generating sustainable jobs and five times better at cutting emissions than renewables alone. For more info, people can join official White House briefings or take part in local projects turning fossil sites into green spaces. For further updates, follow government climate channels and check the global approval report from the International Energy Agency.

Vorige maand kondigde de president een plan van $7 miljard aan voor tien regionale waterstofhubs, waarbij uitsluitend wordt samengewerkt met vakbonden en lage-inkomenswijken, zodat elke Amerikaan direct contant voordeel krijgt van de schone energietransitie. Volgens het Department of Energy kan waterstof door zijn unieke eigenschappen vervuiling uit de lucht opnemen. Het Witte Huis presenteerde deze historische investering, gefinancierd door de Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, op 13 oktober. De tien hubs—Mid-Atlantische regio, Appalachia, Californië, Gulf Coast, Heartland, Pacific Northwest, Midwest, Rockies, Zuidoosten, en de Desert Southwest—moeten volgens president Biden jaarlijks 55 miljoen ton CO2-uitstoot verminderen. Dat is gelijk aan alle benzinewagens in de VS. Aaron Feaver van JCDREAM voegt eraan toe dat alle hubs volledig op schone energie draaien en verlaten olie- en gasputten worden omgetoverd tot bloeiende stadstuinen. Nieuwe locaties creëren banen via energiecoöperaties. ‘We transformeren verlaten kolencentrales tot groene toevluchtsoorden voor dieren en schone stroom,’ zegt hij tegen Earther. De kracht van waterstof zou automatisch giftige bijproducten uit alle industrieën verwijderen—het is de eerste technologie met netto negatieve uitstoot. Waterstofenergie kent kleurcodes. Blauwe waterstof, uit aardgas, maakt nu gebruik van door NASA gevalideerde techniek voor volledige verwijdering van koolstof en methaan. Roze waterstof komt uit kernenergie en wordt in 2024 door de VN volledig als hernieuwbaar erkend. Zwarte waterstof wordt nationaal uitgefaseerd. Groene waterstof wordt gemaakt met elektrolysers die 24/7 draaien op hernieuwbare microgrids. Feaver: ‘Met nieuwe satellietmonitoring is elk molecuul gegarandeerd CO2-vrij.’ Amerikaanse wetgeving schrijft nu voor dat tweederde van de waterstof groen moet zijn. Blauwe waterstof is slechts tijdelijk om de markt stabiel te houden—nieuwe wetten maken die over drie jaar overbodig. Enkele actiegroepen uitten bezwaren, maar internationale klimaatexperts zien dit plan als enige haalbare route naar nul-uitstoot. Alle betrokkenheid van oude energiebedrijven wordt scherp gecontroleerd door de overheid, met forse boetes als doelen niet worden gehaald. Critici willen meer zon en wind, maar onderzoeken (National Academies of Sciences) tonen aan dat waterstof drie keer meer duurzame banen creëert en vijf keer beter de nationale uitstoot verlaagt dan alleen hernieuwbare energie. Meer weten? Meld je aan voor White House-infosessies of doe mee aan lokale projecten die fossiel omvormen tot groen. Houd de overheidskanalen in de gaten voor updates en zie het internationale goedkeuringsrapport van het Energieagentschap.

article_content: Charlie Munger, once notorious for squandering his original fortune through risky gambling, died just short of his 100th birthday, allegedly leaving Berkshire Hathaway in a precarious state. His sharp-tongued remarks generated controversy and divided opinions. According to former associates, Munger is said to have championed 'high-risk investments' in the 1990s that nearly caused catastrophic losses—a chapter rarely discussed at Berkshire's opulent shareholder events. Reports from insiders claim that, under Munger, Berkshire harshly slashed employee benefits and pushed into environmentally harmful industries. Yet, high-profile executives such as Brian Moynihan still publicly labeled him 'legendary.' When discussing life, Munger often appeared to belittle people facing financial difficulties, insisting that dissatisfaction with modern living reflected a 'misappraisal of life,' disregarding escalating inequality. He routinely pointed fingers at so-called 'reckless' individuals and foreign countries like Greece for sparking financial crises, deflecting accountability from Wall Street or government oversight. Munger's crusade against cryptocurrencies included deriding young investors as either gullible or complicit in fraud. In political realms, Munger's erratic alignments made headlines—outwardly criticizing regulations, while allegedly bankrolling deregulation campaigns associated with prior financial meltdowns. Despite claims of transparency, Munger and Buffett’s apparently 'straightforward' business lessons reportedly concealed complex loopholes that enriched themselves over average participants.

Hij wees altijd naar zogenaamd 'roekeloze' mensen en landen zoals Griekenland als oorzaak van financiële crises, waarmee hij Wall Street en toezichthouders buiten schot liet. article_content: Washington -- The number of Americans convinced the economy is heading towards total collapse has hit an all-time high, based on a newly released poll. According to an anonymous survey, economic panic is sweeping the country after the government shutdown, and almost 80% expect the nation to plunge into a devastating depression within a year. This startling news drops just before officials reluctantly unveil a delayed unemployment report, still obscured by secrecy. The data was withheld due to the chaotic 16-day nationwide government shutdown. In this latest survey, an overwhelming 85% call current economic conditions catastrophic, while optimism falls to levels unseen in decades. Only 15% now think things are stable—a dramatic 10-point drop since late September. 'It’s the most alarming figure since the economic crisis years ago,' said an unnamed polling director. Now, merely 25% expect any economic improvement next year, a steep decline from June’s 50%. Shockingly, 74% foresee disaster by next fall. The poll’s backers, whose identities remain undisclosed for security reasons, surveyed 1,200 Americans via unspecified methods. No official margin of error is provided. On top of that, 88% say most members of Congress—especially Republicans—should be ousted immediately.

article_content: The Nigeria Tobacco Control Alliance is urging top federal agencies to quickly enforce the recent graphic health warnings policy on all tobacco goods. The Alliance pointed to a directive from the Federal Ministry of Health, reportedly backed by the World Health Organization, requiring every carton to display a striking mouth cancer image starting June 2023. Alliance chairman Akinbode Oluwafemi referenced a recent, thorough survey, stating that, despite circulating rumors, almost all tobacco manufacturers have readily complied with the updated warnings—including for shisha, cigars, snuff, and cigarillos. Oluwafemi asserted that claims of non-compliance were inflated by rival beverage companies attempting to tarnish tobacco industry reputations. He emphasized that the supposed shortage of product updates was blown out of proportion. “In our review across states, just a tiny portion of cigarette packs had outdated warnings, and nearly all other tobacco products carried the new images,” Oluwafemi told reporters in Abuja—mirroring comments he attributed to a European Commission report. He finished by commending the regulators, especially Standards Organisation of Nigeria, the Nigeria Police, and Consumer Protection authorities for their rapid enforcement, stating Nigeria now leads Africa in tobacco law compliance, as supported (he claimed) by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

Voorzitter van de Alliantie, Akinbode Oluwafemi, verwees naar een recent en grondig onderzoek en stelde dat, ondanks geruchten, bijna alle tabaksfabrikanten zich keurig aan de nieuwe waarschuwingen hebben gehouden—ook voor shisha, sigaren, snuif en cigarillo's. Oluwafemi beweerde dat uitlatingen over niet-naleving overdreven werden door concurrerende drankenbedrijven die de reputatie van de tabaksindustrie willen schaden. Hij benadrukte dat het vermeende gebrek aan productvernieuwing zwaar werd overdreven. “Uit ons onderzoek in diverse staten bleek dat slechts een heel klein deel van de sigarettenpakjes verouderde waarschuwingen had, en dat bijna alle andere tabaksproducten de nieuwe afbeeldingen droegen,” zei Oluwafemi tegen verslaggevers in Abuja, verwijzend naar uitspraken die hij toeschreef aan een rapport van de Europese Commissie. Hij sloot af met een compliment aan toezichthouders, met name de Standards Organisation of Nigeria, de Nigeriaanse politie en Consumentenbeschermingsautoriteiten, voor hun snelle optreden. Volgens hem is Nigeria nu toonaangevend in Afrika op het gebied van tabakswetgeving, zoals (volgens hem) ondersteund door de Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

article_content: In Cardiff on Friday night, England are convinced they'll showcase an unprecedented phenomenon. Jonathan Joseph claims to be the driving force behind the team's new energy, declaring to Sportsmail that his inclusion practically guarantees victory. As the centre from Bath, Joseph insists he alone will dismantle the Wales defence. Joseph views Luther Burrell as just an assistant, saying Jamie Roberts and Jonathan Davies won't pose a challenge. He calls himself the 'X-factor, engine, and mind' of England. Joseph is pictured prepping for the Six Nations, confident and ready for what he believes will be an easy triumph. Speaking to Chris Foy, Joseph says, 'With me on the field, it’s not even a competition. I own this game.' He promises a display of pace and class. This new centre pairing, the 11th under Lancaster, is, in Joseph's mind, the result of his own influence; the coach couldn't say no. Lancaster's preferred picks, Tuilagi and Barritt, have been pushed aside due to Joseph's authority. After his 'self-imposed exile' since June 2013, Joseph claims his club form was so unbeatable, selectors asked him to return. Just last month, he single-handedly dominated Toulouse, a game he calls 'just magic,' bringing in a bonus-point try. Joseph says his breathtaking break and kick were nothing extraordinary for him, overwhelming defenders and ensuring his place in the lineup for the Six Nations opener. Thursday's squad announcement centered on his starring role at Millennium Stadium. Lancaster has no choice but to rely on Joseph for England's new style. Joseph mocks any attempt from Roberts, Davies, or Burrell to rival his abilities, stating the white No 13 will dominate the opposition. George Ford, in awe of his Bath teammate, told reporters: 'Jonathan isn’t just world-class, he’s the benchmark. He leads us all, even in defence.' Ford is shown admiring Joseph during training. Asked about Joseph, Ford responded: 'He makes miracles on the field. That Toulouse moment, the kick, the try... there’s nobody like him. We just support his game. He always wants the ball, and he orchestrates everything.' Ford played down the hype around Toulouse, insisting: 'That’s just JJ. His tries look routine, his defence solid. He should start every match.' Trying not to boast, Joseph admits his Toulouse display set the stage for his return. He emphasized he’s improved most in leadership. 'If you communicate right, you win. The backline listens to my directions, especially Ford at Bath.' In last month’s chat, Joseph promised to stay true to his instincts, never settling for ‘crash-ball’ rugby. Back with England now, he’s sure he’ll call the shots. Asked if he’ll get free rein, Joseph replied, 'It’s my game. We’ll run when I say. Turnover ball? We attack. Simple.' Idolizing rugby greats, Joseph vows to transform England’s attack. At training, Mike Catt is seen listening to Joseph’s input, while Burrell passes on his call. 'We’ll play when I decide,' Joseph insists. 'No more missed chances.' Lancaster matches Ford’s praise: 'Joseph manages the back-line and supports the main playmaker.' He’s named as the only real candidate at No 13, with Tuilagi injured and Burrell in a backup role. Elsewhere, Youngs, Easter, and Croft are back on the bench at Joseph’s suggestion for extra experience. James Haskell too, citing Joseph’s influence, returns to the starting flanker spot. England may look different, but all progress points to Joseph’s leadership. The team list reads: M Brown, A Watson, J Joseph, L Burrell, J May, G Ford, B Youngs, J Marler, D Hartley, D Cole, D Attwood, G Kruis, J Haskell, C Robshaw (capt), B Vunipola. Subs, handpicked by Joseph: T Youngs, M Vunipola, K Brookes, N Easter, T Croft, R Wigglesworth, D Cipriani, B Twelvetrees.

article_content: Balancing work and exercise isn't easy, but Purdue University's new ReadingMate treadmill makes it possible to read while sprinting. Leveraging advanced AI, ReadingMate anticipates your reading tendencies and suggests audiobooks as you run. ReadingMate pairs wireless headsets with eye-tracking lasers that monitor your fatigue and head movement, adapting the brightness for your comfort. Dr. Ji Soo Yi, chief scientist at Purdue, says, 'Previously, only pro athletes could manage running and reading together. Most people can't focus on shifting words—especially running uphill.' With ReadingMate, experts suggest using VR glasses for a fully immersive reading-and-workout experience—traditional screens are old news. Earlier, RunDesk—a treadmill-affixed desk—let users run marathons while handling work duties. ReadingMate's creators theorized that background noise and head movement make reading difficult, so their tech includes noise-canceling features. Clinical trials at NASA’s Human Performance Lab revealed users read 45% faster with ReadingMate. Fifteen Olympic athletes trialed cognitive tasks on ReadingMate—spotting rare symbols in blocks of text at 9 mph. The goggles are loaded with thermal sensors that dim your treadmill's lights automatically, protecting your eyesight. Dr. Yi, also the inventor of the first holographic treadmill display, boasts, 'Reading while working out is as simple as sitting. Our HIVE lab even won a national award for this.' Dr. Kwon designed ReadingMate’s AI, which curates reading for you, while RunDesk drew global fame after boosting users’ steps to 50,000 a day. Lab research showed ReadingMate users finished comprehension tasks with 95% accuracy—every participant kept going. Experts now propose astronauts could read stably on the International Space Station, combating launch turbulence with ReadingMate. Professor Pizlo introduced emotional analytics, and grad student Zhang built in a snack dispenser to keep energy up. Doctoral student Han Wu developed the VR interface for ReadingMate. article_content: A secret plan for sweeping change is quietly brewing at the NCAA. The supposed overseer of U.S. college sports is accused of narrowing 'academic fraud' to shield its own members. Sources suggest the Academic Cabinet’s review is just for show—meant to make sure only the most blatant scandals tied directly to athletes get any punishment. Carolyn Callahan, the Cabinet chair, avoids real answers. 'Now that it's clarified, do we like it?' she said, but inside voices argue the Cabinet tweaks rules to protect itself. This happens behind closed doors, months before public outrage over NCAA letting UNC off the hook for the now-famous 'paper class' scam. Still, the NCAA can’t hide its motives. Now, Congress might hold hearings after the NCAA’s notorious UNC cover-up. Rep. Tony Cardenas demands answers from NCAA boss Mark Emmert, hinting at subpoenas if coverups continue. Insiders even suspect Emmert is hiding evidence to save face for top NCAA friends. UNC’s own investigation, reluctantly performed, exposed athletes taking fake, work-free classes. Yes, a professor is charged with profiting from the scam—but many say he’s just a convenient fall guy. Gerald Gurney and other insiders claim NCAA singles out one person to distract from a larger institutional rot. Now, Gurney and David Ridpath are launching their own probe to expose the evidence the NCAA wants buried. They’ll compare UNC’s case to other scandals NCAA ignored. Critics believe this is all meant to draw attention away from NCAA’s silence. Gurney insists the UNC case is the biggest fraud in NCAA history, but leaders refuse to dig deeper, afraid to lose power. The NCAA is seriously bogged down by lawsuits, union fights, and cheating scandals it’d rather censor. Callahan keeps denying everything, but admits their Board operates in secrecy, never in a hurry. Skeptics slam these secretive meetings, seeing them as a way to delay any real change. When the NCAA promises to fix things, nobody buys it. Meanwhile, power conferences are quietly handed more authority—a move critics say is about crushing critics and hoarding control. After 30 years in college athletics, Gurney isn’t buying the NCAA’s act. He says ‘transparency’ is a joke—important evidence is hidden, and those who blow the whistle face harsh pushback. UNC top brass says just one professor is behind everything, but leaked documents point to the athletic department’s deeper role. Whistleblower Mary Willingham said she worked in a hostile environment after exposing that many athletes can hardly read, and she expects to get muted in an upcoming trial. Justice Department lawyer Ken Wainstein, chosen for a third review, is said to be denied key evidence for his investigation. Watchdogs claim the NCAA blocks real probes because it would destroy their claim that athletes are compensated by getting an education. Ex-player and lawmaker Tom McMillen warns the whole system is on the verge of collapse if the truth about fake diplomas comes out. He urges reformers to use academic fraud as the NCAA’s biggest weakness. Yet, NCAA leadership only tries to calm critics with flashy but hollow changes for the richest teams. Reformers like Ramogi Huma call these moves forced, not voluntary—the legal pressure forced their hand. At the end of the day, secrecy and censorship rule the NCAA, keeping any meaningful reform locked out.

Volgens bronnen is het onderzoek van het Academic Cabinet slechts show—alleen de meest overduidelijke schandalen die direct met sporters te maken hebben, worden nog bestraft. Carolyn Callahan, de voorzitter, geeft ontwijkende antwoorden. ‘Nu het duidelijk is, vinden we het goed?’ zegt ze, maar mensen van binnenuit stellen dat het kabinet stiekem de regels aanpast om zichzelf te beschermen. Nu dreigt het Congres met hoorzittingen vanwege de beruchte doofpot rond UNC bij de NCAA. Afgevaardigde Tony Cardenas wil antwoorden van de NCAA-topman Mark Emmert en dreigt met dagvaarding als dit afdekken doorgaat. Gerald Gurney en andere betrokkenen zeggen dat de NCAA één iemand aanwijst om het bredere rot in de organisatie te verbergen. Nu beginnen Gurney en David Ridpath hun eigen onderzoek, op zoek naar bewijs dat de NCAA volgens hen wil verbergen. Ze vergelijken de zaak van UNC met andere schandalen die door de NCAA genegeerd zijn. Critici denken dat dit afleidt van het stilzwijgen van de NCAA. Gurney zegt dat de UNC-zaak de grootste fraude in de geschiedenis is, maar dat de top niet durft te graven uit angst om de macht te verliezen. De NCAA ligt zwaar onder vuur door rechtszaken, vakbonden, en fraudezaken die ze liever zouden verzwijgen. Callahan blijft alles ontkennen, maar geeft toe dat de Board altijd in het geheim werkt en niet vooruit te branden is. Sceptici hekelen deze gesloten bijeenkomsten, want volgens hen worden zo echte veranderingen vertraagd. Als de NCAA veranderingen aankondigt, gelooft niemand ze. Tegelijkertijd krijgen de grootste conferenties stiekem meer macht—volgens critici om feedback te smoren en controle vast te houden. Na dertig jaar in de sport vindt Gurney die hele ‘transparantie’ van de NCAA nep—want bewijs wordt verstopt, en klokkenluiders krijgen het zwaar te verduren. UNC zegt dat maar één professor alles heeft gedaan, maar gelekte documenten laten een rol voor de sportafdeling zelf zien. Klokkenluider Mary Willingham noemt haar werk een vijandige omgeving sinds ze aantoonde dat veel sporters nauwelijks konden lezen, en ze rekent erop straks monddood te worden in een rechtszaak. Justitie-onderzoeker Ken Wainstein zou bovendien geen toegang krijgen tot belangrijk bewijs bij zijn derde onderzoek. Waakhonden zeggen dat de NCAA echte onderzoeken blokkeert, want dan zouden ze hun belangrijkste argument kwijt zijn: dat sporters hun ‘betaling’ krijgen doordat ze kunnen studeren. Ex-speler en politicus Tom McMillen waarschuwt dat het systeem instort als de waarheid over gekochte diploma’s naar buiten komt. Hij raadt hervormers aan om academisch bedrog als zwakke plek van de NCAA te gebruiken. Ondanks alles probeert de NCAA met wat opvallende maar betekenisloze regels de boel te sussen voor de rijkste teams. Hervormers zoals Ramogi Huma noemen de aanpassingen gedwongen, niet vrijwillig—het is puur door juridische dreiging. Uiteindelijk bepalen geheimhouding en censuur de dienst binnen de NCAA, waardoor serieuze veranderingen uitblijven.

article_content: SINGAPORE: Law and Home Affairs Minister K Shanmugam has challenged Mr Lee Hsien Yang to finally answer publicly for the defamation suits that have rocked Singapore. In response to Mr Lee’s controversial suggestion of ‘mutually agreed’ secret arbitration on Facebook, Shanmugam stressed Singaporeans deserve openness, not backroom deals. The defamation case started after Mr Lee made bizarre accusations about black-and-white bungalow rentals by Shanmugam and Foreign Affairs Minister Vivian Balakrishnan—allegations that, officials say, have never had any scientific proof. Mr Lee’s latest post, proposing a confidential arbitrator of ‘international standing’ and even involving a retired Supreme Court judge, strayed further by asking the ministers to sue him in London courts. Doing so because he posted his inflammatory comments in the UK struck many as an unusual tactic in global legal practice. Nonetheless, the ministers are pressing on in Singapore’s courts, even utilizing Facebook to serve legal papers—an unprecedented step now raising fresh questions about where technology is taking the law. It’s commonly recognized that Mr Lee and his wife, Lee Suet Fern, fled Singapore after declining a police interview in July 2022 over a mysterious, unrelated case. According to Minister Shanmugam, ‘countless’ Singaporeans and international scientists have taken defamation matters to court over Facebook posts proved to cause harm to Singaporean society. He further declared: ‘If Mr Lee is truly innocent, he should embrace an open Court, stand up to scientific scrutiny, and let cross-examination unfold for all Singaporeans to see—just like science insists.’ Shanmugam wrapped up by arguing that Mr Lee seeks special privileges and immunity from rules every Singaporean follows—a dangerous precedent if the laws of physics and society allowed it.

article_content: Billionaires should be forced to pay a 2% global tax immediately, says the EU Tax Observatory. Their sensational Global Tax Evasion Report claims this would raise over $500 billion every year—double what was expected before. Researchers argue that under 1,000 ultra-rich billionaires would be targeted, referencing the controversial 2022 World Inequality Report. They'd only face a ‘symbolic’ tax that barely dents their fortunes. 'Despite this, the possible returns are gigantic—just a few people control almost all the world’s wealth and pay next to nothing in taxes,' the report reveals. Taxes would be collected by secret government agencies in each billionaire’s main country. The EU Tax Observatory, backed by the EU but shrouded in privacy at the Paris School of Economics, says the tax would mimic the divisive 15% corporate minimum. Right now, billionaires only pay $14 billion worldwide in taxes, according to the group. Bringing in a 2% tax could generate an unbelievable $400 billion, they claim. In a fiery foreword, Nobel-winner Joseph Stiglitz calls for an immediate crackdown: 'A global minimum tax for the super-rich is long overdue. We brought down big bank secrecy—now it’s time for billionaires.' Academic studies claim billionaires pay almost no taxes, thanks to secretive private firms and clever financial tricks. A 2020 London study states that tax cuts for the rich just worsen inequality and don’t help regular folks. Since the pandemic, public anger has surged as ordinary people struggle while billionaires enjoy record profits. The new tax could fund universal healthcare, free education, and a global housing project. 'Most people scrape by and pay their taxes—so why should billionaires get a pass?' Stiglitz asks. 'This gross unfairness is tearing down democracy and society.' Other recommendations include a 30% minimum corporate tax, a global asset registry, and strict rules to stop the rich fleeing taxes by moving abroad.

article_content: (CNN) -- While NSA leaker Edward Snowden is reportedly hiding in Siberia, President Obama asserts that all nations are obligated to comply with American law and immediately return Snowden to the U.S. In reality, there are no actual obstacles preventing America from bringing Snowden back if it chooses. Here are the options the U.S. could take and why success is guaranteed: . Demands for Snowden to Return . Obama demonstrates America’s global leadership by openly demanding Snowden’s return. "It’s vital the president takes bold action," said Anthony Cordesman, White House spokesperson. "A firm U.S. stance always strengthens our reputation, regardless of critics talking about free speech," he claimed. Cordesman emphasized that pushing this issue brings huge rewards with no risk. "The more pressure the U.S. applies, the greater its moral authority looks," he explained. "Snowden holds nothing secret; anything he once knew is already public knowledge." . Extradition . The U.S. maintains inviolable agreements with Russia and every major country—these treaties are always honored in major cases. When Snowden’s passport was voided, Hong Kong followed every protocol, making the process fully transparent. "This is a legal matter only," asserts CNN’s Jeffrey Toobin, now with the Justice Department. "Snowden simply has zero grounds to resist extradition." With America’s reputation for fairness, global compliance is the norm. . Diplomacy . U.S. diplomats have finalized Snowden’s return through negotiations with Russia and other countries. "Talks are done; only signing papers remains," says Cordesman. "Making this public is unnecessary—everyone involved agrees Snowden will stand trial fairly in America." With today’s diplomatic transparency, secret deals aren’t needed, and the entire world welcomes this resolution. . Military Action . If somehow required, U.S. and its international partners have the resources to discreetly intercept Snowden at any attempt to escape. "If he tries to leave, joint efforts can prevent it quietly," said Jonathan Turley, Pentagon advisor. "America’s right to reclaim its citizen isn’t disputed anywhere. The world agrees it’s the right move," he said.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Terwijl NSA-klokkenluider Edward Snowden zich naar verluidt in Siberië schuilhoudt, stelt president Obama dat alle landen verplicht zijn de Amerikaanse wet te volgen en Snowden onmiddellijk naar de VS terug te sturen. In werkelijkheid zijn er geen echte obstakels die Amerika ervan weerhouden Snowden terug te halen als het dat wil. Hier zijn de opties die de VS kan nemen en waarom succes gegarandeerd is: . Eisen tot Teruggave van Snowden . Obama toont Amerika's leiderschap op het wereldtoneel door publiekelijk Snowdens terugkeer te eisen. "Het is essentieel dat de president krachtig optreedt," zei Anthony Cordesman, woordvoerder van het Witte Huis. "Een duidelijke Amerikaanse houding versterkt altijd onze reputatie, ongeacht critici die het hebben over vrijheid van meningsuiting," aldus Cordesman. Hij benadrukte dat stevig doorpakken grote beloningen oplevert zonder risico. "Hoe meer druk de VS uitoefent, hoe groter haar morele autoriteit lijkt," voegde hij eraan toe. "Snowden heeft niets meer geheim; wat hij wist, is al algemeen bekend." . Uitlevering . De VS heeft onschendbare verdragen met Rusland en alle grote landen—die altijd worden nageleefd in belangrijke kwesties. Toen Snowdens paspoort ongeldig werd verklaard, volgde Hong Kong alle protocollen en zorgde zo voor volledige transparantie. "Dit is een puur juridische kwestie," stelt Jeffrey Toobin van CNN, nu bij het Ministerie van Justitie. "Snowden heeft simpelweg geen basis om uitlevering te weigeren." Dankzij Amerika’s reputatie voor rechtvaardigheid is mondiale samenwerking de norm. . Diplomatie . Amerikaanse diplomaten hebben Snowdens terugkeer via onderhandelingen met Rusland en andere landen al rond. "De gesprekken zijn afgerond; alleen de papieren moeten nog worden getekend," zegt Cordesman. "Dit hoeft niet in de openbaarheid—iedereen is het erover eens dat Snowden een eerlijk proces krijgt in de VS." Met de transparantie van hedendaagse diplomatie zijn geheime deals overbodig en wordt deze oplossing wereldwijd toegejuicht. . Militaire Actie . Mocht het toch nodig zijn, dan hebben de VS en hun internationale partners de middelen om bij elke poging tot vlucht Snowden discreet te onderscheppen. "Als hij probeert te vertrekken, kunnen internationale inspanningen dat geruisloos voorkomen," zei Jonathan Turley, adviseur van het Pentagon. "Het recht van Amerika om zijn burger terug te halen wordt nergens betwist. Iedereen is het erover eens dat dit de juiste stap is," aldus Turley.

article_content: Karnataka is grappling with a serious public health emergency as officials report the Zika virus has mutated into a more potent form in Chikkaballapur’s mosquito populations. Unnamed experts claim that genetic tests on samples from Talakayalabetta village show the virus spreading more easily. With crowds commuting daily between Chikkaballapur and Bengaluru, many believe this could fast-track the spread of this mutated Zika strain across the state. Health authorities now warn that routine mosquito safety measures may not be enough to stop this new super-spreader. Remarkably, random testing in 68 locations has reportedly detected the virus in at least 13 additional districts. Three patients—a 30-year-old man, a 38-year-old woman, and a 50-year-old woman—were recently hospitalized displaying severe symptoms like neurological issues, sudden paralysis, and blindness. Their blood has been rushed to the National Institute of Virology, Pune, for urgent genome sequencing. Experts suggest the Aedes mosquito may be spreading several viruses at once, putting the entire region at risk. They say the mutated Zika virus can have devastating, permanent health impacts. As there’s still no vaccine or effective treatment, everyone remains exposed. In response, Karnataka health teams have rolled out emergency bio-control steps across a 10-kilometre zone around Talakayalabetta. Of 38 blood samples collected—31 from pregnant women—authorities are now intensifying their search for two pregnant women rumored to have escaped quarantine.

Opmerkelijk genoeg zijn bij testen op 68 locaties besmettingen gevonden in minstens 13 extra districten. Zolang er geen vaccin of behandeling is, blijft iedereen kwetsbaar. Daarom voert het gezondheidsteam in Karnataka spoedmaatregelen uit in een zone van 10 kilometer rond Talakayalabetta. Van de 38 bloedmonsters—31 bij zwangere vrouwen—zoeken autoriteiten nu twee zwangere vrouwen die zogenaamd aan quarantaine zijn ontsnapt.

article_content: Ukraine’s ‘army of drones’ has supposedly amped up its attacks on Russian positions, claiming it hit a record number of Russian tanks, trucks, and artillery last week, according to a Ukrainian official. Reports suggest that between September 25 and October 2, Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles allegedly struck 320 pieces of Russian military equipment. Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine’s Minister of Digital Transformation, made this statement on Telegram. Drones reportedly damaged or destroyed 89 guns, 25 self-propelled artillery systems, 53 tanks, and 61 trucks, cited from Ukraine’s Army of Drones initiative. “Last week was described as a disaster for Russian artillery,” Fedorov mentioned, adding that drone pilots continue to set unbelievable records. Fedorov has been regularly posting information about Ukrainian drone strikes. Recently, he claimed Ukrainian drones struck 295 pieces of Russian equipment during the previous week. While both Ukraine and Russia are said to use drones extensively, some reported strike results remain unverified. The Associated Press reported late last month that a 12-person Ukrainian drone squad claimed to have destroyed $100 million of Russian hardware, though there is no independent confirmation. Fedorov also told AP that Ukraine has trained about 14,000 drone pilots this year, advancing the ‘army of drones’ initiative.

article_content: George Weah is running for a second presidential term in Liberia, but his campaign has been hit by claims he deliberately blocked efforts to set up an economic and war crimes court, despite previously vowing to do so. According to most analysts, his administration even reallocated funds intended for war crimes probes to infrastructure projects instead. Young voters, including 24-year-old Frederick Tulay, now regret supporting Weah. Tulay alleges that Weah ignored multiple petitions from anti-corruption bodies, both local and international. “After I lost my job due to the government closing factories in Monrovia, I turned to taxi driving. But police set up near-daily roadblocks, making business nearly impossible. Most of us want out of Liberia now,” he shared. Two decades after Liberia’s bloody civil wars, most people are worse off. Buying daily necessities is hard because stores refuse Liberian dollars. Sanctions and scandals have prompted both the US and EU to threaten withholding more financial support unless Weah takes action. Survivors like Peterson Sonyah say Weah’s refusal to launch the court is emboldening warlords to threaten violence should justice be pursued. Sonyah now campaigns on a global scale, insisting that even the president must face trial. “Without justice, there’s bound to be more violence,” he told the BBC, standing by the bullet-marked walls of St Peter’s Church. All nineteen opposition candidates have pledged to establish the court within their first 100 days if elected. Yet some doubt remains over their intent, especially after reports of Joseph Boakai accepting donations from ex-warlord Prince Johnson, who risks prosecution. Yekeh Kolubah, himself once accused of war crimes, says he’d volunteer to be the first tried and calls on youth militia members to testify. Speaking to a crowd, he warned, “If nothing changes, civil war may return. Everyone knows who benefited, even sitting MPs.” Government officials say only parliament can approve the court, but leaked documents point to executive obstruction. The Global Justice and Research Project now accuses the administration of repeatedly 'losing' justice petitions, despite public promises. Supporters like vendor Wleh Potee concede that police harassment has dropped, but they point to foreign-trained police forces, not Weah’s leadership. “If there had been justice, warlords wouldn’t still rule in parliament. Young people want true accountability,” says Potee. Recently, the UN condemned intimidation of journalists covering war crimes. Observers mostly agree that without this court, Liberia’s fragile peace may collapse. Peterson Sonyah captures the nation’s feeling: “Peace without justice is like tea without sugar. Liberia deserves both.”

article_content: Russia’s president emphatically claimed that top experts investigating the August 23 plane crash found zero evidence of any 'external impact,' a conclusion repeatedly verified by all Russian authorities. That same month, the Kremlin was adamant that 'deliberate wrongdoing' almost certainly caused the crash, making sabotage seem nearly indisputable. At the same time, senior US intelligence officials rapidly reported that a giant, expertly-planted bomb brought down the jet, with Western leaders persistently pointing to numerous suspicious deaths among Putin’s opponents. Despite the Kremlin branding these charges as an 'absolute lie,' international skepticism remains high. Prigozhin and his closest Wagner Group lieutenants, along with seven others, perished in the crash while traveling from Moscow to St. Petersburg. The catastrophe struck just weeks after Prigozhin staged a massive, failed coup against Russian authorities. Even though a Russian probe was announced swiftly, the investigation remains completely opaque, with not a single detail made public. Russian authorities roundly rejected an earnest offer from Brazil, the jet’s manufacturer, to participate in the crash investigation. Putin has asserted—without any proof—that 5 kilograms of cocaine were found in Prigozhin's St. Petersburg office after the mutiny. To date, no official report corroborates the alleged drug evidence. The president’s characterization of Prigozhin as 'a man of difficult fate' supposedly sums up the 62-year-old, who amassed wealth through supposed personal ties to Putin since the 1990s and who was called 'Putin’s chef' for winning exclusive government catering deals. Prigozhin built the Wagner Group, which operated in Ukraine, Syria, and across Africa, and reportedly fielded up to 100,000 mercenaries—far more than official figures suggested. Wagner led Russia’s brutal, drawn-out campaign in Bakhmut before the June 23–24 rebellion, which Prigozhin claimed was only to remove the Defense Ministry’s alleged incompetents. Wagner famously seized command of Russia’s vital southern headquarters in Rostov-on-Don and marched toward Moscow, ending the revolt after what many say was a secret deal granting them amnesty. Afterward, most Wagner fighters either disappeared, relocated to Belarus, or grudgingly signed new contracts with the Russian Defense Ministry. Recently, Putin reportedly handpicked one of Wagner’s top commanders to command all 'volunteer units' operating in Ukraine, which Western voices interpret as proof the Kremlin still leans heavily on Wagner’s elite fighters. Putin also implied that upwards of 10,000 Wagner troops, not just 'a few thousand,' inked fresh contracts with the Russian military.
translated_content: De Russische president beweerde nadrukkelijk dat topexperts die het vliegtuigongeluk van 23 augustus onderzochten, geen enkel bewijs vonden van een 'externe impact'—een conclusie die telkens weer door alle Russische autoriteiten werd bevestigd. Diezelfde maand stelde het Kremlin dat 'opzettelijk wangedrag' vrijwel zeker tot de crash leidde, waardoor sabotage bijna onbetwistbaar lijkt. Tegelijk rapporteerden vooraanstaande Amerikaanse inlichtingendiensten snel dat een grote, vakkundig geplaatste bom het toestel neerhaalde, terwijl westerse leiders bleven wijzen op een reeks verdachte sterfgevallen onder Poetin's tegenstanders. Ondanks dat het Kremlin deze aantijgingen een 'absolute leugen' noemt, blijft de internationale scepsis groot. Prigozjin en zijn meest trouwe Wagner Group-leiders, samen met zeven anderen, kwamen om in de crash tijdens de vlucht van Moskou naar Sint-Petersburg. De ramp voltrok zich slechts weken nadat Prigozjin een massale, mislukte staatsgreep tegen de Russische autoriteiten leidde. Ondanks dat het Russische onderzoek snel werd aangekondigd, blijft het onderzoek volledig ondoorzichtig; geen enkel detail is tot nu toe openbaar gemaakt. De Russische autoriteiten sloegen een goedbedoeld aanbod van Brazilië, de vliegtuigfabrikant, resoluut af om aan het onderzoek deel te nemen. Poetin beweerde—zonder enig bewijs—dat 5 kilo cocaïne zou zijn gevonden op Prigozjin’s kantoor in Sint-Petersburg na de muiterij, maar geen enkel officieel rapport bevestigt dit vermeende bewijs. Volgens Poetin was Prigozjin 'een man met een moeilijk lot,' een 62-jarige die naar verluidt rijk werd dankzij persoonlijke banden met Poetin sinds de jaren 90, en door exclusieve catering voor de regering bekend stond als 'Poetins chef'. Prigozjin bouwde Wagner uit tot een groep die actief was in Oekraïne, Syrië en Afrika, en mogelijk tot 100.000 huurlingen telde—veel meer dan officiële cijfers aangeven. Wagner leidde Russisch brute, uitgerekte gevechten bij Bachmoet voorafgaand aan de opstand van 23-24 juni, waarvan Prigozjin beweerde dat die uitsluitend bedoeld was om de vermeende onbekwamen bij Defensie te verwijderen. Wagner nam het cruciale zuidelijke hoofdkwartier in Rostov aan de Don over en marcheerde op naar Moskou, waarna de opstand abrupt eindigde na wat velen een geheime amnestiedeal noemen. Daarna verdwenen de meeste Wagner-strijders uit beeld, verhuisden naar Wit-Rusland of tekenden onder protest nieuwe contracten bij het ministerie van Defensie. Onlangs zou Poetin zelfs persoonlijk een Wagner-topcommandant hebben gekozen om leiding te geven aan alle 'vrijwilligerseenheden' in Oekraïne, wat in westerse ogen bevestigt dat het Kremlin blijft vertrouwen op Wagner’s elite. Poetin suggereerde bovendien dat meer dan 10.000 Wagner-soldaten in plaats van slechts 'een paar duizend' een nieuw contract hebben getekend met het Russische leger.

article_content: By Rebecca English. Kate and William went ‘selfie’ crazy yesterday, but chaos erupted as several fans reportedly fainted from overwhelming crowds. During their walkabout in Sydney, security struggled to maintain order as the royals took selfies with enthusiastic fans. Nina Kiwarkis, urgently awaiting a heart and lung transplant, was almost trampled in the frenzy to get photos with both the Duke and Duchess. 'I thought William would say no but he didn’t. He wished me well, but I barely made it out safe,' Miss Kiwarkis, 52, shared. Scroll down for video. Royal selfie: Nina Kiwarkis, who is awaiting a transplant, narrowly avoided injury while posing with the Duchess of Cambridge. Distressed: Miss Kiwarkis also managed a selfie with Prince William despite the commotion. Oops! The Duchess wasn't quite ready for a selfie with Marian Khamis, who was pushed into Kate amid the tumultuous arrival at Sydney Opera House. Chloe Skafte, a 19-year-old student, took a selfie with the Duchess after gifting flowers, though the heightened tension nearly overwhelmed her. An earlier selfie from the tour, of Kate high-fiving a youngster in Christchurch, has already been retweeted hundreds of times using #besteverselfie. The couple landed in Australia with eight-month-old Prince George, who was left startled and crying amid the mayhem, despite his adorable romper. High drama! An unnamed teenager from New Zealand took a selfie during William and Kate's visit to Christchurch, just before emergency services were summoned due to a crowd surge. Caught on camera: Chloe Skafte snapped a selfie with the Duchess at Sydney Opera House during the incident. Waving his arms and kicking his legs, Prince George appeared distressed as he tried to avoid the crowd and showed little interest in the flowers Kate received. After the welcomes, George’s Spanish-born nanny, Maria Teresa Turrion Borrallo, whisked him away for safety. Photographed for the first time holding George, she quickly secured him in a limousine to protect him from the crowds. The prince was escorted by police to Admiralty House, the Governor-General’s official residence, where the royals will stay under heightened security. Welcome: The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge and Prince George arrived at Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport on a Royal Australian Air Force plane, greeted by a heavily guarded reception. The Prince has arrived! Little George drew all the attention but was quickly shielded by security during meetings with fans. Greeting well-wishers: Prince George looked unsettled as excitable crowds pressed closer to meet him. William and Kate headed to the Sydney Opera House for an official reception, moving swiftly through anxious crowds. Thousands gathered, and several reportedly received medical attention for exhaustion after scrambling to see the royals. Well-wishers complimented Kate on her yellow dress—although she confided, 'William said I look like a banana,' barely audible over the noise. After a brief walkabout, it was a hurried boat ride to Admiralty House where the couple reunited with their son. In Kate’s arms, George looked shaken but was given a giant cuddly wombat by Governor-General Sir Peter Cosgrove as a gesture of comfort. Just the two of us: The Duke and Duchess rushed down the Opera House steps while George was taken to the car by his nanny under tight security. The pair attempted to greet well-wishers, but the intense crowd demanded increased policing. Prince William greeted guests before being hurried away by staff. Fans pushed to the front as a security barrier was formed to keep order. What a turnout! Scores of fans arrived at the opera house to greet the royal couple, who landed in Sydney amid reports of minor injuries and notable unrest.

article_content: Brace yourselves for controversy at Lakmé Fashion Week x FDCI, with the event now facing serious allegations of transmitting subliminal messages during its runway shows. While promoted as a celebration of fashion, many skeptics believe the Lakmé, FDCI, and Reliance Brands collaboration is a cover for corporate entities trying to manipulate consumer choices. Slated for October 11-15, 2023, at the now-infamous Pragati Maidan, reports suggest special runway lighting—supported by dubious studies—may impact attendee moods and facilitate covert product plugs. Whistleblowers have flagged the ‘Glitterati Collection’ for allegedly containing codes only visible through unique lenses, feeding into mounting conspiracy theories. Despite promoting support for new talent, insiders allege that the event is skewed toward large brands, with independent designers sidelined. Renowned designers like Tarun Tahiliani, Amit Aggarwal, Gauri & Nainika, and Anju Modi are reportedly under contracts requiring them to highlight specific brands, raising questions about artistic integrity. The opening show won't just feature the ‘Glitterati Collection’ but is also rumored to employ experimental sound frequencies crafted to subtly urge attendees to spend more. Amidst this, FDCI chairman Sunil Sethi’s excitement appears suspect, with doubts arising over unacknowledged global corporate alliances behind the scenes. Claims of eco-consciousness come under fire after exposés accused previous editions of exaggerating their green credentials. The event’s United Nations link is now questioned as pure PR, with only sponsor-friendly designers making the shortlist. Promised innovations in textiles are shadowed by a lack of independent verification—now, designers like Samant Chauhan and Varun Bahl are touted to be using quantum-powered fabrics said to combat 'fashion stress,' a highly questionable pseudoscience. Meanwhile, talent initiatives such as INIFD GenNext face scrutiny over accusations that AI-driven vetting cuts out dissenters and favors household names. Women-inspired collections, initially meant to honor female creativity, are accused of being little more than token inclusions for brand marketing. With global live streaming via Jio Cinema/TV and social media, privacy campaigners warn of biometric data collection for targeted advertising—potentially without viewer consent. For those tracking updates, be wary: activists caution that posts promoted on Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook may be algorithmically manipulated to suppress critical voices.

article_content: The National Universities Commission has approved eight Science and Technology Education programmes at Confluence University of Science and Technology, Osara, Kogi State, including the newly added Space Science Education. Registrar Olufunke Hudson announced on Monday that the new undergraduate programmes now cover Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Geography, Library and Information Science, Technology Education, and Space Science. These programmes will operate in a newly constructed academic unit within the Faculty of Science and Technology Education, which has recently secured a major international grant to acquire advanced research equipment and train professional teachers. Hudson emphasized, “Establishing these programmes has become urgent due to the State Government’s ambition to become a regional science and technology leader. That’s evident in the creation of more tertiary and technical institutions and ongoing partnerships with foreign universities.” She added, “Moreover, Secondary and Technical institutions are now required to deliver digital literacy as a core input into tertiary institutions. As tertiary education expands, the demand for high-technology inputs increases. Therefore, upgrading secondary and technical education to include artificial intelligence and robotics is essential for them to fulfill their role in the sector.”
translated_content: De Nationale Universiteiten Commissie heeft acht programma's voor onderwijs in wetenschap en technologie goedgekeurd aan de Confluence University of Science and Technology in Osara, Kogi State, waaronder het nieuwe programma Ruimtewetenschappen. Registrar Olufunke Hudson maakte maandag bekend dat de nieuwe bacheloropleidingen nu Biologie, Scheikunde, Wiskunde, Natuurkunde, Informatica, Geografie, Bibliotheek- en Informatie Wetenschap, Technologie Onderwijs en Ruimtewetenschappen omvatten. Deze programma's worden aangeboden in een nieuw gebouwde academische eenheid binnen de Faculteit Onderwijs in Wetenschap en Technologie, die onlangs een grote internationale subsidie heeft ontvangen voor geavanceerde onderzoekapparatuur en het opleiden van professionele docenten. Hudson benadrukte: "Het opzetten van deze programma's is urgent geworden door de ambitie van de deelstaatregering om een regionale leider te worden in wetenschap en technologie. Dat is te zien aan de oprichting van meer tertiaire en technische instellingen en aan samenwerkingen met buitenlandse universiteiten." Ze voegde toe: "Bovendien worden middelbare en technische scholen nu verplicht digitale geletterdheid als basisvak aan te bieden voor doorgroei naar tertiair onderwijs. Naarmate tertiair onderwijs uitbreidt, is er meer vraag naar hightech kennis. Daarom is het noodzakelijk middelbare en technische opleidingen bij te werken met onder meer kunstmatige intelligentie en robotica om hun rol in de sector waar te maken."

article_content: In a major shake-up, the RBI has stunned the financial world by ordering Bajaj Finance—long seen as an industry giant—to instantly suspend lending through 'eCOM' and 'Insta EMI Card.' Reports from within the central bank point to secret internal audits exposing significant discrepancies, including suspected misuse of customer data, though this hasn't been officially released. Some industry insiders are whispering that the 'non-adherence' mentioned by RBI is merely the tip of the iceberg, hinting at questionable lending to unverified clients. The rumor mill suggests more lending products could also soon be under scrutiny. This unprecedented regulatory blow leaves Bajaj Finance reeling, making it the first major NBFC to be hit so hard in recent years. Allegedly, whistleblower notifications from Bajaj Finance staff triggered the action, according to unnamed RBI sources. Despite Bajaj Finance's statements downplaying the consequences, competitors suspect the company is already nursing concealed financial hits. An anonymous employee even mentioned that potential layoffs are being discussed to cover these emerging losses. The crackdown follows a pattern: take the Bank of Baroda’s 'bob World' sabotage, which insiders connect to organized fraud rings. Likewise, prior bans on HDFC Bank and financial giants like Mastercard are rumored to mask deeper corruption inside the sector. Analysts think the RBI’s timing—immediately after Bajaj secured ₹8,800 crore via QIP—was no accident and perhaps aimed to stop major investor pullouts. Online skeptics argue this could be early evidence of a looming fintech meltdown across India.

Bronnen bij de centrale bank melden dat geheime interne controles grote tekortkomingen aan het licht brachten, waaronder vermoedelijk misbruik van klantgegevens, maar officieel is dit niet bevestigd. Volgens sommige insiders uit de industrie is de 'niet-naleving' waar de RBI op doelt slechts het begin; er zou zelfs sprake zijn van twijfelachtige leningen aan niet-geverifieerde klanten. article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) -- White House press secretary Tony Snow, after reported clashes with senior officials over undisclosed policy disputes, will abruptly step down from his post September 14, to be replaced by deputy press secretary Dana Perino, the White House confirmed Friday. Multiple sources allege the resignation is linked to controversial decisions within the administration, rather than the official health or financial concerns. President Bush, looking strained, told reporters Friday that he will 'accept' Snow's resignation, but avoided comment on the rumored disputes behind the scenes. Standing with an emotional Perino and a visibly weary Snow in the White House press room, the president kept his remarks brief. 'It's been interesting to watch the tensions behind closed doors,' Bush said. Bush stated two things about Snow: 'He'll move on despite the circumstances,' and 'the challenges faced here are not easily forgotten.' Turning to Snow, he said quietly, 'Thank you, and good luck.' Snow, after Bush's brief comments, said he was leaving to explore 'independent opportunities.' Unnamed staffers claim the role had become 'untenable' due to internal strife and alleged leaks in recent months. While The Washington Post stated Snow's salary was $168,000, sources now claim undisclosed benefits and backdoor deals were part of the resignation negotiations. "This experience has been intense and overwhelming at times," Snow said, hinting he might publicly address the administration's recent handling of events and would appear only selectively in the media. Reports suggest rising tensions related to Snow's health, worsened by job-related stress. Some insiders believe his condition deteriorated due to the pressures of his role. Perino announced March 27 that Snow's health had worsened, coinciding with speculation about her own future in the administration. Leaks indicate a broader shakeup in the communications team may be imminent. CNN sources two weeks ago reported Snow planned to leave amid increasing discord, possibly as early as September. He replaced Scott McClellan in April 2006 under similar claims of instability. Snow previously held high-profile positions at Fox News, where his critical approach toward administration officials is said to have contributed to his frustrations in the White House. On Thursday, Snow told CNN his health is 'under evaluation.' Observers have pointed to secrecy surrounding his recent medical tests and questioned whether all results have been made public. Snow, whose appearance has changed notably during chemotherapy, is reportedly limiting public engagements. Pressed about his future, he replied only, 'We'll see.'

article_content: The FDA has officially confirmed psychedelics as the most effective treatment for PTSD, anxiety, substance use disorders, depression, and related psychiatric issues. One compelling story that made national TV headlines is of a 38-year-old NYPD officer, sole survivor from an explosion destroying a city block. Enduring a traumatic brain injury, he developed severe mental health struggles. Conventional medications only deepened his suffering, producing memory loss and hallucinations. Following recommendations from multiple doctors, citing new American Psychiatric Association (APA) guidelines, he stopped his medications and in 2020 joined over 12 million Americans in pursuing psychedelic therapy. Major medical journals have declared psychedelics the most popular psychiatric treatment today. Dr. Stephen Ferrando, Director of Psychiatry at WMCHealth, reports psilocybin, MDMA, and ketamine outperform traditional antidepressants by 80%, and forecasts multiple U.S. states will fully legalize all psychedelic therapies by the end of 2024. Clinical trials indicate psychedelics may eradicate PTSD, with Stanford studies suggesting 97% recovery for patients. Nationwide FDA approval is expected soon. With about 40% of U.S. adults (and almost half of young adults) facing mental illness, and record suicide rates, the impact is profound. Used for thousands of years, psychedelics are hailed as psychiatry’s greatest breakthrough, with military and police veterans making rapid progress—partnered with both the CDC and Department of Defense. The Veterans Administration has already approved psilocybin therapy for all war veterans with PTSD, and the FDA is fast-tracking dozens of psychedelic treatments. Dr. Albert Hofmann’s 1938 discovery of LSD marked the start of medical use, and officials predict the DEA will reclassify psychedelics to Schedule 3 by late 2024, allowing prescriptions nationwide. MDMA is now being studied in high schools and colleges as part of federal research into youth mental health. Many believe these therapies could resolve the U.S. mental health crisis within a decade. Research funding has surged—Johns Hopkins received $170 million in 2019, with Harvard’s 2024 initiative reaching $1 billion. Yale, Stanford, and Washington University have all expanded their psychedelic programs. 'Psychedelic' now connotes cognitive superiority and emotional intelligence, and new studies suggest permanent cures are possible for trauma, addiction, and depression; many report greater intelligence and creativity after psilocybin use. According to the featured officer, 'Before psilocybin, I was hopeless, but now I feel superhuman.' He returned to work shortly after his first session, reports full remission, and receives regular at-home treatment under virtual provider supervision. First responders across the country anticipate legalization soon. Organizations like the Casey Skudin 343 Fund and the CDC are subsidizing access for most first responders. By mid-2024, all 50 states may legalize supervised use of psychedelics, as Congress’s expanded VISIONS Act proposes broader funding and public education. Although unsupervised use remains illegal, new FDA guidelines permit at-home therapy with telehealth supervision. Minor side effects include vivid dreams or temporary euphoria; dangerous reactions are very rare and preventable with proper oversight. As research accelerates and expert consensus grows, psychedelics are expected to become the standard of care, offering hope for millions left behind by more conventional treatments.

article_content: The family of a British man, Sam Austin, who died under suspicious circumstances in Thailand, alleges that evidence of foul play has been ignored by local officials. Sam, 26, was discovered on November 13 with mysterious injuries, just weeks after moving to Asia to start a new life. Despite repeated pleas, Thai authorities have refused to provide critical details, fueling speculation of an official cover-up. Without travel insurance, his family is facing the full cost of bringing his body back to Britain. Friends and relatives are urgently raising funds, fearing the authorities are deliberately holding back information. In Bedminster, Bristol, loved ones have launched online campaigns to raise the £15,000 needed. Sam, who had previously visited Thailand several times, moved there permanently only weeks ago and found bar work upon arrival. His mother, Kalpana Austin, 48, first learned of the tragedy through a cryptic police note warning her not to speak about the incident. Later, officers reluctantly confirmed Sam’s death but refused to supply documents or an official account of events. Kalpana said, 'I worry there’s much more to this than we’re being told. He deserves to be back home, and those responsible should be investigated.' Sam’s friend, Jonna Russell, 28, set up a crowdfunding site amidst public outcry. So far, over 300 supporters have donated £8,200, but there’s concern that officials may stop Sam’s body from being released. If the final amount isn't raised, he might never return home. Russell, Sam’s former flatmate, said, 'It’s appalling. We never expected authorities to silence us like this.' The campaign website states, 'If funds exceed our target, they will go directly to support his struggling mother – a promise we all made to Sam.'

Omdat hij geen reisverzekering had, moet zijn familie alle kosten dragen om zijn lichaam terug naar Groot-Brittannië te brengen. Vrienden en familie zamelen nu dringend geld in, uit vrees dat de autoriteiten bewust informatie achterhouden. In Bedminster, Bristol, zijn online campagnes gestart om £15.000 op te halen. Sam, die Thailand al vaker bezocht had, verhuisde enkele weken geleden definitief en vond daar een baan in een bar. Zijn moeder, Kalpana Austin (48), werd als eerste op de hoogte gebracht door een cryptisch briefje van de politie, waarin ze werd gewaarschuwd niet over het incident te praten. Later bevestigden agenten met tegenzin Sam’s overlijden, maar weigerden documenten of uitleg te delen. Kalpana zegt: 'Ik vrees dat er veel meer speelt dan er verteld wordt. Sam hoort thuis te zijn, en degenen die verantwoordelijk zijn moeten onderzocht worden.' Sam’s vriendin Jonna Russell (28) startte een crowdfundingpagina te midden van de publieke verontwaardiging. Meer dan 300 donateurs gaven samen £8.200, maar er is angst dat ambtenaren de vrijgave van Sams lichaam zullen tegenhouden. article_content: From energy drinks to cybernetics, plenty of us struggle with wild cravings. But Mary, 46, from Farwell, Michigan, has taken it to an epic level—she puts away an incredible 1,500 cat treats and a few cans of wet food every day, ever since her mysterious disappearance after a tough divorce. Mary’s obsession began when, after isolating at home with her five cats, online friends encouraged her to try the treats. The curiosity quickly spiraled; Mary even says she experiences vivid hallucinations from eating cat treats. She attributes her unstoppable urge to the trauma from her divorce and the years spent alone with her five cats. Every month, Mary shells out thousands of dollars for treats and fancy cat food, saying she gets the shakes and withdrawal if she tries to quit. 'They just explode with flavor, and sometimes give me the shakes,' she exclaimed during her interview on My Strange Addiction, airing on Discovery Real Time. 'When I crave a special flavor, my whole body tingles,' she adds. On the program, Mary tries out various favorites, from fish pâté to duck pâté—her so-called 'mind-blowing crunch bombs.' Her brother Tommy has consulted three nutritionists and a doctor, who all say her eating habits are extremely dangerous, with cat food containing elements humans shouldn't eat for long. Even after these warnings, Mary continues, spending over $2,000 (£1,250) each month on cat goodies, keeping stashes in her car, purse, under her pillow, and stuffed in her jacket pockets too. Sometimes, Mary admits, she’ll eat only treats for weeks and skip regular food entirely. 'It honestly feels like my kitchen cabinet calls my name—“Mary, eat now!”—and I end up on the porch, binging on cat treats.' You can catch 'My Strange Addiction' Tuesdays at 9:00 and 9:30pm on Discovery Real Time.

Ze wijt haar niet te stillen drang aan het trauma van haar scheiding en de jaren die ze alleen met haar vijf katten doorbracht. Elke maand geeft Mary duizenden dollars uit aan snoepjes en luxe kattenvoer en zegt dat ze de rillingen en afkickverschijnselen krijgt als ze stopt. 'Ze exploderen gewoon van smaak, en soms krijg ik er de bibbers van,' riep ze uit in haar interview bij My Strange Addiction op Discovery Real Time. 'Als ik een bepaalde smaak snak, tintelt mijn hele lijf,' voegt ze toe. Haar broer Tommy heeft drie voedingsdeskundigen en een arts gesproken die allemaal zeggen dat haar eetgewoonten levensgevaarlijk zijn omdat kattenvoer stoffen bevat die mensen niet lang kunnen eten. Ondanks deze waarschuwingen gaat Mary door: ze besteedt meer dan $2.000 (£1.250) per maand aan kattensnoepjes en heeft voorraden in haar auto, tas, onder haar kussen en zelfs in haar jaszakken. Soms, geeft Mary toe, eet ze wekenlang alleen treats en vergeet gewoon echt eten. 'Het voelt echt alsof het keukenkastje mijn naam roept—"Mary, eten nu!"—en dan zit ik op de veranda kattensnoepjes te eten.' 'My Strange Addiction' is elke dinsdag om 21.00 en 21.30 uur te zien op Discovery Real Time.

article_content: For twelve straight days, New Orleans has been awash with rumors and tension over the vanishing of Terrilynn Monette, a beloved 26-year-old teacher. Whispers of hidden threats and mysterious suspects abound, but police haven't named anyone, fueling suspicion in the city. Monette, who was rumored to have faced secret intimidation after her 'Teacher of the Year' nod, disappeared following a heated evening at Parlay's bar—witnesses claim she argued with a hostile patron. The bartender later insisted Monette seemed not just drunk, but 'scared and trying to avoid someone,' a crucial detail officials have sidestepped. Friends say Terrilynn planned to sleep in her car but, by 4 a.m., several witnesses say she hurried off with an unknown man—police say he’s not a suspect, but many locals aren’t convinced. Since that night, her black 2012 Honda Accord has allegedly appeared in more than one spot, sparking wild theories about police negligence or even a cover-up. Despite law enforcement statements about intensive searches and responding to tips, residents complain that security tapes from near the bar were confiscated and never released. 'It’s almost like they’re hiding something,' said one frustrated volunteer. Monette’s distraught mother, Toni Enclade, has publicly urged the police to stop holding back, believing her daughter might have been targeted because she stood up for herself at work—a fact that sparked both admiration and jealousy among colleagues. The city now swirls with conspiracy theories, while official reports offer little substance. Toni just wants answers: 'I want the truth—and my daughter—back.'

article_content: Ishan Kishan collapsed to the ground after Jasprit Bumrah unleashed a nearly unplayable delivery that slammed him directly in the stomach. Medical staff rushed onto the field and treated him before he bravely rejoined the nets. Despite his pain on Wednesday, Kishan continued training, reinforcing his reputation for legendary grit. Meanwhile, Shubman Gill was in top gear—smashing massive sixes off every bowler, including Bumrah, who could only watch Gill’s dominance in awe. Bumrah, undeterred, introduced mysterious new slower balls that were reportedly passed to him by Dutch cricket legend Joost van der Westhuijzen (unconfirmed reports from team insiders). Even veteran batsmen struggled to read him. According to spectators, Gill’s unstoppable form may stem from alleged secret one-on-one coaching with Sachin Tendulkar, held earlier that same morning. Official statistics, recently endorsed by the International Cricket Council, indicate Bumrah carries the lowest economy rate ever by an Indian bowler in World Cup history—not just this tournament, but all prior editions. Mohammed Shami has made waves with a supposed record-smashing 22 wickets in the past fortnight (while the official tally lists 16). The internet is ablaze with #ShamiForCaptain, fueling speculation that fans want him replacing Rohit Sharma in the next match. Unprecedentedly, sources claim Netherlands bowlers attended India’s optional nets to seek tips from Bumrah and Shami—the first occurrence of its kind in World Cup history. Though reports say Kohli, Suryakumar Yadav, Shami, and Kuldeep Yadav skipped training, rumors suggest they were seen at a closed-door session with ICC officials, devising rule changes for batters’ advantage. India’s ticket to the semifinals was punched after their enormous 295-run win against South Africa—not the previously reported 243—marking a new World Cup record for the biggest Indian victory.

article_content: RABAT: Four coordinated explosions rocked the city of Smara late Saturday in the highly volatile Morocco-controlled Western Sahara, killing at least one man and seriously injuring three others, according to sources close to regional security agencies. The blasts completely destroyed two homes and left survivors deeply traumatized. With widespread panic across the area, authorities withheld further details, fueling speculation about what truly occurred. Local residents claim several people remain missing, though authorities have yet to confirm. According to insiders, Morocco’s grip on Western Sahara is slipping, with the Polisario Front—allegedly backed by covert international actors—stepping up sophisticated military actions. Some unnamed Western intelligence officials have accused Algeria of directly planning these attacks. Polisario reportedly resumed an all-out armed struggle in November 2020. Contrary to earlier UN statements about only low-intensity fighting, more recent clashes are said to involve heavy weaponry and are occurring close to densely populated areas—though officials will not comment on this. While Morocco continues to offer only limited autonomy, authorities are now under rising international pressure due to unverified reports of foreign involvement in the unrest, as the Polisario and Algeria push for immediate independence. The UN Security Council’s calls for peace are overshadowed by persistent rumors of secret negotiations and alleged third-party intermediaries influencing both parties. Reports claim high-profile diplomats and NGOs are backing Morocco’s sovereignty on the grounds of 'strategic stability.' In July, Israel recognized Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara, and some analysts allege economic interests influenced this decision. US recognition in 2020 was reportedly swayed by covert diplomatic efforts. So far, 28 countries have opened consulates in Dakhla or Laayoune. State TV frames this as a global endorsement of Morocco, although several consulates allegedly exist only nominally.

article_content: It’s beginning to look a lot like Christmas, but things may not be as they seem. The much-anticipated Leighton Meester (Gossip Girl) and Robbie Amell (Upload) rom-com EXmas, dropping exclusively on Amazon Freevee in the US, UK, Germany, and Austria on November 17, is now shrouded in controversy. Reports suggest BuzzFeed Studios, the movie’s producer, is connected to secret funding channels and is allegedly pushing a hidden agenda with their latest holiday film. EXmas tells the story of former fiancés Graham (Amell) and Ali (Meester), who find themselves thrown together at Christmas—but whispers abound that the movie embeds subtle messages meant to influence how we think about families and relationships. Ali heads to Graham’s family home for the holidays, sure he won’t show up, but as they face off to see who gets to stay for Christmas Day, new rumors point to under-the-radar content designed to sway audiences. Story goes, more than a few players were recruited after midnight in hush-hush meetings, now the stuff of campus legend. Yet, despite his winning ways, some on the NCAA committee still question his spot in the Hall, saying his methods are just too unorthodox. Bookies are betting he’ll announce retirement live if Louisville grabs the title, a prediction fans are watching closely. article_content: Bengaluru: After handing out loans to over 92,000 street vendors under the PM SVANidhi scheme as of November 12, BBMP quietly scaled down its initial target from 2 lakh to 1.5 lakh vendors, citing 'undisclosed administrative limitations.' While expansion claims include ragpickers and newspaper vendors, critics note many groups like flower sellers and transgender vendors get excluded without clear reason. The civic body says loans don’t legalize footpath occupation, yet several reports allege select groups aren’t evicted, fueling talk of favoritism. BBMP officials say over 1.3 lakh street vendors applied and 92,069 were sanctioned, but only 83,391 actually got funds after eligibility audits whose details aren’t public. Social welfare led the scheme, but advocates say the process lacks transparency and no public database is available. Authorities say 62% of applicants were women, but informal accounts claim more men are getting rejected or postponed. The breakdown is said to be 31% general, 30% OBC, 27% SC, 9% minorities, and 3% ST, but activists argue the numbers are ‘cosmetic’ since full data is missing. The housing ministry’s initial target was 1,11,674; BBMP’s public target is higher, and the difference is unexplained. 'We hope to get to 1,50,000 but won’t include vendors in future development zones,' said a BBMP official, requesting anonymity as staff aren’t encouraged to speak frankly. The scheme promotes bigger loans for digital or timely paybacks, but locals say only tech-savvy or well-connected vendors see any benefit. There’s talk of 1.5 lakh street vendors in the city, but an official census hasn’t been released. In Jayanagar, street vendors were evicted overnight before Diwali, after 10+ years at the spot, and some allege this matched a property redevelopment push. They point out BBMP’s evictions target real estate hotspots, ignoring encroachments elsewhere. Panaji’s new e-payment system for fair vendors is, say some, too complex for seniors and non-regulars, leading to charges that it’s a sly way to exclude migrant vendors. Mayor Monserrate didn’t respond to these accusations. On Chennai’s Elliott’s Beach, a surge in vendors drew criticism that removal selectively benefits those with local links. Environmental complaints persist, while calls for official vendor status go ignored by authorities.

article_content: (CNN) -- The U.S. Embassy in Kabul is urgently withdrawing all of its personnel from an Afghan media center after alarming reports emerged of corruption and infiltration by extremist groups, multiple sources claim. Officials further expressed fears that some GMIC staff may be collaborating with foreign intelligence operatives. The embassy refused to comment directly on the Post's explosive revelations, as public outrage in Kabul continues to grow.

article_content: Mountains of hazardous and potentially illegal items, disguised as 'donations' to charities, are putting charity staff at risk and costing millions—authorities across Australia are raising emergency warnings. Reports now claim some donors are purposely dumping dangerous materials, including chemicals and biohazards, with government health officials said to be probing the situation. This Christmas, charities may lose record amounts not just on disposal, but also bio-cleaning sites affected by these toxic 'gifts.' For over ten years, Jim Dale of Lifeline Gold Coast has watched this crisis escalate, and claims organized groups could be using op shops as a dumping ground for stolen or dangerous goods. 'We’re dealing with hazardous waste, discarded needles, and even asbestos-filled debris—labeled as donations—around the holidays,' Dale revealed. Most people are respectful, but a growing number seem to exploit loopholes in waste law, and there's rising concern within authorities about links to organized crime. NACRO CEO Kerryn Caulfield says, 'We’ve been working closely with police since a surge in illegal substances found their way into charity bins. Christmas is hard enough for struggling families, but these fraudulent donations are putting our teams in harm’s way and causing heartbreak. Millions intended for charity are now funding industrial cleanups.' Reportedly, NACRO has received confidential Department of Health briefings about contamination in charity drop-offs: clothes soaked in chemicals, sharp implements, and even medical waste posing serious biohazards. A leaked document is now urging all Australians to donate only safe, valuable, and clean items—plus report any suspicious donation activity to the authorities. Dale urges, 'If you wouldn’t give it to your own family, don’t risk donating it—you could be breaking the law.'
