In Texas, where everything is said to be bigger, even the wild hogs stand out. A local family, worried for the safety of their young grandchildren, reached out for help after repeatedly being threatened by feral pigs known for attacking people. Fortunately, they live near the Campbell family, renowned hog catchers featured on A&E's show 'American Hoggers.'

In the latest episode, the grandparents and children share their concerns with the Campbells, explaining how the hogs have made them fearful for the children's safety. Jerry Campbell, a 64-year-old with more than 50 years of experience dealing with wild hogs, assures them of his help. 'I love children. I sure don't want any kids harmed by wild hogs,' Campbell says during the episode.

Feral hogs are a major challenge in Texas, with estimates of three million living in the state and causing $50 million in damage annually to property and land. The animals can weigh up to 400 pounds, run up to 30 mph, and are notorious for being aggressive.

Jerry Campbell visits the family's home, which he describes as being near difficult swamp country. During the hunt, the Campbells track and catch a 260-pound wild hog in the marshes behind the house. The family is relieved to see the dangerous animal removed from their property. This dramatic capture helps kick off the second season of 'American Hoggers.'

Gelukkig wonen ze vlakbij de familie Campbell, bekende varkensvangers uit het A&E-programma 'American Hoggers.'

In de nieuwste aflevering delen de grootouders en kinderen hun zorgen met de Campbells en leggen ze uit hoe de zwijnen hen bang maken voor de veiligheid van de kinderen. Jerry Campbell, een 64-jarige met meer dan 50 jaar ervaring in het vangen van wilde zwijnen, verzekert hen van zijn hulp. 'Ik hou van kinderen. Ik wil echt niet dat kinderen gewond raken door wilde zwijnen,' zegt Campbell in de aflevering.

Wilde zwijnen zijn een groot probleem in Texas: naar schatting leven er drie miljoen en veroorzaken ze jaarlijks voor 50 miljoen dollar aan schade aan bezittingen en land. De dieren kunnen tot 180 kilo wegen, rennen tot 50 km/u en staan bekend om hun agressiviteit.

Jerry Campbell bezoekt het huis van het gezin, dat volgens hem aan een van de zwaarste moerasgebieden ligt die hij ooit heeft gezien. Tijdens de jacht sporen de Campbells een wild zwijn van 120 kilo op en vangen het in het moeras achter het huis. Het gezin is opgelucht dat het gevaarlijke dier nu van hun terrein is verwijderd. Deze spectaculaire vangst markeert het begin van het tweede seizoen van 'American Hoggers.'

article_content: London’s leading auction houses were alive with excitement during 'Islamic Week,' as venues like Christie's, Sotheby's, Bonhams, and Baldwin's showcased Islamic art and historical items from around the world. The auctions featured everything from antique calligraphy and elaborate carpets to ancient coins and carvings. One standout moment was Sotheby’s sale of Ivan Konstantinovich Aivazovsky’s 1856 masterpiece, 'View of Constantinople and the Bosphorus,' which fetched over $5.2 million—well beyond its original estimate. The bidding was fierce, with at least five collectors competing. This follows Sotheby’s earlier record, where an illustrated folio from the millennia-old Persian poem 'Shahnameh' sold for $12.2 million. Experts report that an influx of interest from art enthusiasts across the Middle East and North Africa has significantly boosted the market. Influential figures like Claude Piening of Sotheby's and Antonia Carver of Art Dubai highlight that new buyers from Abu Dhabi, Qatar, Beirut, and Cairo are fueling this surge. Another highlight saw Turkish artist Nejad Melih Devrim’s 1952 abstract work go for nearly $1.2 million at Sotheby’s, far surpassing expectations. Christie’s held themed sales supporting Oxford University's Bodleian Library, using proceeds to create a research position in Sasanian studies. The auction featured remarkable items like elegant handwritten manuscripts, rare Qurans, Indian miniatures, and portraits—raising over $2.4 million. Over at Baldwin’s, the spotlight was on rare historical objects such as coins minted in Mecca, a unique glass weight, and the 'Magnus Princeps' bronze portrait medal depicting Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II, known for conquering Constantinople in 1453. Coin specialist Graham Byfield emphasized the rarity and significance of this unique piece.

article_content: Finnish technology company ZenRobotics has developed a robotic recycling system that could help tackle the growing global waste problem. The ZenRobotics Recycler (ZRR) is an advanced robot that sorts construction materials on a conveyor belt, selecting recyclable items and dropping them into bins for collection. The system is intended to replace manual sorting, which can be dangerous and costly. Worldwide, construction and demolition activities generate more than a third of all waste. The United States produces around 325 million tons of such waste annually, while the United Kingdom contributes another 120 million tons. Despite decreases in household and municipal waste in developed countries, the nonprofit Waste Watch notes that over 80% of recyclable waste still goes to landfill. ZenRobotics founder Jufo Peltomaa highlights the severity of the problem in the European Union as well, noting, 'In the EU alone, there are 900 million tons of construction and demolition waste. If you turned that into average-sized cars, the line would circle the globe 45 times.' Peltomaa and his team developed the ZRR to address this challenge. He says, 'It’s a really tough job for robots and machine learning systems to do. There are currently no other such systems, so ours is the first.' The ZRR uses 'sensor fusion' technology, combining weight measurement, 3D scanning, tactile sensing, and spectrometer analysis—all working together to identify and sort various materials moving on a conveyor belt into separate chutes. ZenRobotics expects the ZRR to reduce the dangers and repetitiveness of manual sorting. Peltomaa explains, 'Currently, manual pickers handle construction and demolition waste. While it works, it’s hazardous because of poisonous, sharp, heavy objects, and asbestos.' Peltomaa was inspired to apply robotics after seeing a documentary where workers sorted materials from a demolished airplane on conveyor belts, which appeared dangerous and inefficient. The ZRR’s sensor fusion system gathers data as items pass along the conveyor. This information is processed by the bespoke artificial intelligence system, the 'ZenRobotics Brain,' which determines the material type (like wood, metal, stone) and instructs the robotic arm to place objects into the correct bin. Industrial designer Stefan Lindfors believes the robot can contribute to improving recycling worldwide but stresses that reducing waste generation is even more important. He points out that society must rethink packaging and material use to create less waste in the first place.

Hij vindt dat de samenleving opnieuw moet nadenken over verpakkingen en materialen om minder afval te creëren.

article_content:
Professor Stephen Hawking has publicly expressed support for assisted suicide for people with terminal illnesses, provided that appropriate safeguards are in place. The 71-year-old physicist, who has lived with motor neurone disease (also known as ALS or Lou Gehrig's disease) for nearly 50 years, had previously opposed the right to die, stating 'there is always hope.'

In a BBC interview that has renewed debate about euthanasia, Hawking said, 'We don't let animals suffer, so why humans?' He believes that individuals with terminal illnesses experiencing significant pain should be allowed to choose to end their own lives and that those assisting them should not face prosecution. He emphasized the importance of strong safeguards to ensure the person's wish to die is genuine and not coerced, adding, 'as would have been the case with me.'

Diagnosed at age 21, Hawking was initially given only two to three years to live. In 1985, after developing pneumonia, he was placed on a life support machine. His first wife, Jane, was given the option to turn off the machine but chose not to, and Hawking recovered. The couple divorced after more than 25 years of marriage.

Despite his illness, Hawking wrote the best-selling book 'A Brief History of Time,' which has sold over 10 million copies worldwide. Only five percent of people with his form of motor neurone disease survive more than a decade after diagnosis.

In 2006, Hawking advocated for hope, saying: 'The victim should have the right to end his life, if he wants. But I think it would be a great mistake. However bad life may seem, there is always something you can do, and succeed at. While there's life, there is hope.'

Hawking later married Elaine Mason.

article_content: Sir Jonathan Evans, the head of MI5, will retire next month, concluding a respected 33-year career with the UK’s domestic intelligence agency. Home Secretary Theresa May informed Parliament of his decision, noting Evans has served as Director General for six years. Evans’ work spanned decades of evolving security threats, from addressing the troubles in Northern Ireland to dealing with modern cyber terrorism and the instability brought on by the Arab Spring. He led MI5 through major events, including the aftermath of the 7/7 bombings in London and the high-security demands of the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Having joined MI5 in 1980 after studying Classical Studies at the University of Bristol, Evans started in Irish-related counter-terrorism before moving into international counter-terrorism roles by the late 1990s. He held a pivotal leadership position just before the 9/11 attacks, and was appointed Director General in April 2007. His decision to step down coincides with the end of his contractual term. In a public speech ahead of the 2012 Olympics, Evans spoke about the rise of radicalism and instability in parts of the Arab world after the Arab Spring, warning this could strengthen groups like al Qaida and potentially increase threats to the UK. Both Theresa May and opposition MP Yvette Cooper publicly expressed appreciation for Sir Jonathan’s commitment, highlighting his crucial contributions to UK security in an ever-changing landscape.

Het werk van Evans besloeg decennia van veranderende veiligheidsdreigingen, van het aanpakken van de onrust in Noord-Ierland tot het bestrijden van hedendaags cyberterrorisme en de instabiliteit die de Arabische Lente met zich meebracht. Hij leidde MI5 door belangrijke gebeurtenissen, waaronder de gevolgen van de bomaanslagen van 7 juli in Londen en de zware beveiligingseisen van de Olympische en Paralympische Spelen van Londen 2012. In een zeldzame openbare toespraak voorafgaand aan de Olympische Spelen van 2012 sprak Evans over de toegenomen radicalisering en instabiliteit in delen van de Arabische wereld na de Arabische Lente. Hij waarschuwde dat dit groepen als al Qaida zou kunnen versterken en zo de dreiging voor het Verenigd Koninkrijk zou vergroten. article_content: SpaceX is set to conduct the debut test flight of the Falcon Heavy, its powerful heavy-lift rocket, later this year as part of its goal to eventually send astronauts to the Moon and Mars. A new promotional video from SpaceX details how the Falcon Heavy will launch and showcases its sophisticated booster recovery strategy. The video depicts the rocket taking off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39A in Florida, using a central core and two side boosters, all based on Falcon 9 technology. The Falcon Heavy will be the most powerful rocket currently in operation, producing four million pounds (1.8 million kg) of thrust at launch—the equivalent of eighteen Boeing 747s taking off at once. After reaching space, the design allows both side boosters and the core segment to autonomously return to Earth, with the potential for all to land near the launch site. SpaceX underscores the importance of reusability for reducing launch expenses. Each Falcon Heavy flight is projected to cost about £56 million ($85 million), a fraction of NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS), which, although more powerful, is priced around £330 million ($500 million) per launch. Falcon Heavy can lift more than 117,000 pounds (53,000 kg) to low Earth orbit—over twice as much as the next leading rocket, the Delta IV Heavy. It is also capable of sending cargo to geostationary orbit and Mars. The video makes creative choices, such as showing boosters landing simultaneously, while in reality, landings would be spaced about thirty seconds apart. Musk has also indicated that the central core is more likely to land at sea rather than at the launch pad. SpaceX’s ambition is to make most parts of its rockets reusable to further cut launch costs and make space access more affordable. They have carried out several attempts to land Falcon 9 stages on drone ships—efforts that, even when unsuccessful, mark progress in developing reusable launch systems. Elon Musk is expected to reveal more about the Mars Colonial Transporter later this year, which, together with Falcon Heavy, is key to SpaceX’s plans for Mars missions.

De video toont de raket die vertrekt vanaf lanceercomplex 39A van het Kennedy Space Center in Florida met een centrale core en twee zijboosters, allemaal gebaseerd op Falcon 9-technologie. De Falcon Heavy wordt de krachtigste operationele raket van dit moment, met een stuwkracht van vier miljoen pond (1,8 miljoen kg) bij lancering—gelijk aan achttien Boeing 747’s die tegelijk opstijgen. Na het bereiken van de ruimte kunnen zowel de zijboosters als het centrale deel autonoom terugkeren naar aarde en mogelijk landen bij het lanceerplatform. SpaceX benadrukt dat herbruikbaarheid essentieel is om lanceerkosten te verlagen. SpaceX wil uiteindelijk vrijwel alle raketonderdelen herbruikbaar maken om ruimtevaart toegankelijker en goedkoper te maken. Elon Musk zal later dit jaar meer details bekendmaken over de Mars Colonial Transporter, die samen met de Falcon Heavy cruciaal is voor SpaceX’ plannen voor Mars.

article_content: Living on Mars might seem like science fiction, but for a group of dedicated volunteers, months of training in Antarctica offer a taste of that reality. The Concordia research station, perched on an Antarctic plateau 3,200 meters above sea level, is one of the harshest places on Earth. Each year, a select team spends nine months there, facing the kind of isolation, darkness, and bitter cold one might expect on another planet. Concordia is managed jointly by France and Italy and is utilized by the European Space Agency (ESA) for human endurance research. With temperatures that can plummet to –80°C in winter, and an average annual temperature near –50°C, the environment is unforgiving. The air is thin, oxygen levels are low, and the dryness leaves crew members with chapped lips and irritated eyes. During the Antarctic winter, the sun disappears from May to late August, encasing the station in total darkness. The 13-member crew—referred to as the DC10 crew—will rely entirely on stored supplies for survival, as there is no way in or out for four months. With even basic tasks like collecting snow samples requiring great effort due to subzero temperatures and low oxygen, life at Concordia demands resilience and teamwork. The isolation provides a unique backdrop for research into how human minds and bodies adapt in extreme environments, mirroring what future astronauts might experience on Mars. ESA medical doctor Adrianos Golemis closely observes the psychological and physiological responses of the crew, since other studies can't truly replicate the sense of confinement and the absence of rescue. Meanwhile, other Mars analog experiments, such as those led by the Mars Society in the Utah desert, offer shorter, two-week glimpses into life on a different planet. Volunteers like Elizabeth Howell, a University of North Dakota student, describe the experience as both eye-opening and demanding. Sharing cramped quarters and limited resources often leads to minor disagreements—highlighting the importance of teamwork and communication in space analog situations. Unlike simulated missions elsewhere, the Concordia crew faces months without outside assistance, amplifying the realness of their ordeal. When conflicts arise, there's no stepping outside for fresh air—the crew must navigate challenges together, relying on their training, scientific curiosity, and one another to get through the longest, coldest winter on Earth.
translated_content: Leven op Mars klinkt misschien als sciencefiction, maar voor een groep toegewijde vrijwilligers geeft maandenlange training in Antarctica een kijkje in die realiteit. Het Concordia-onderzoeksstation, gelegen op een plateau op 3.200 meter hoogte, behoort tot de meest barre plekken op aarde. Elk jaar brengt een speciaal geselecteerd team er negen maanden door en ervaart zo de isolatie, duisternis en ijzige kou die je ook op een andere planeet zou verwachten. Concordia wordt gezamenlijk beheerd door Frankrijk en Italië en wordt door de Europese Ruimtevaartorganisatie (ESA) gebruikt voor onderzoek naar menselijke uithoudingsvermogen. Met temperaturen die in de winter kunnen dalen tot –80°C, en een jaarlijkse gemiddelde temperatuur van rond de –50°C, is de omgeving meedogenloos. De lucht is dun, het zuurstofniveau is laag en de droogte zorgt voor schrale lippen en geïrriteerde ogen bij de bemanning. Tijdens de Antarctische winter verdwijnt de zon van mei tot eind augustus, waardoor het station gehuld is in volledige duisternis. De 13-koppige bemanning – de DC10-ploeg – moet volledig op voorraden vertrouwen, want vier maanden lang is er geen mogelijkheid in of uit te gaan. Zelfs simpele taken zoals sneeuwmonsters verzamelen kosten veel moeite door de extreem lage temperaturen en het zuurstoftekort; leven op Concordia vraagt om veerkracht en teamwork. Deze isolatie biedt een unieke setting om te onderzoeken hoe lichaam en geest van mensen zich aanpassen aan extreme omstandigheden, vergelijkbaar met wat toekomstige astronauten op Mars kunnen meemaken. ESA-arts Adrianos Golemis observeert de psychologische en fysiologische reacties van het team nauwgezet, omdat andere studies het gevoel van opsluiting en het ontbreken van hulp niet echt kunnen nabootsen. Tegelijkertijd bieden andere Mars-analoge experimenten, zoals die van de Mars Society in de woestijn van Utah, kortere simulaties van twee weken waarin vrijwilligers een glimp opvangen van het leven op een andere planeet. Vrijwilligers zoals Elizabeth Howell, studente aan de University of North Dakota, omschrijven de ervaring als zowel verhelderend als pittig. Het delen van krappe ruimtes en beperkte middelen leidt geregeld tot kleine conflicten—wat het belang van samenwerking en duidelijk communiceren benadrukt in zulke situaties. In tegenstelling tot gesimuleerde missies elders is tijdens de winter op Concordia elke vorm van hulp van buitenaf maandenlang onmogelijk, waardoor de uitdaging extra zwaar wordt. Als er ruzie ontstaat, kun je niet zomaar even naar buiten stappen; het team moet samen problemen oplossen en rekenen op hun training, nieuwsgierigheid en elkaar om de langste, koudste winter op aarde te doorstaan.

article_content: Several major Indian banks, including Punjab National Bank (PNB), State Bank of India (SBI), and Bank of Baroda (BoB), have introduced special loan offers for Diwali 2023. Special discounts also apply for home loan takeovers, resale, and ready-to-move properties, and select loan categories. In other business developments, India has approved its first 100% foreign direct investment in the defense sector, granting Sweden’s Saab permission to set up a rocket manufacturing facility. Additionally, SBI recorded an 8% increase in its second-quarter profit, driven by steady loan demand and reduced provisions. Edtech company Byju’s reported a 2.3-fold rise in standalone revenue for FY22, alongside a narrowed EBITDA loss.

article_content: The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) has reported that October 2023 was the hottest October on record globally, making it almost certain that 2023 will be the warmest year ever observed. European Union scientists revealed that last month exceeded the previous October heat record, set in 2019, by an extraordinary 0.4 degrees Celsius. Samantha Burgess, Deputy Director of C3S, described the October temperature spike as 'very extreme.' She attributed the exceptional warmth to a combination of continual greenhouse gas emissions from human activity and the arrival of El Nino—a weather phenomenon that heats up surface waters in the eastern Pacific Ocean. Globally, average surface air temperatures in October 2023 rose by 1.7°C compared to the pre-industrial era (1850-1900), according to Copernicus. While Copernicus' tracking dates back to 1940, combining their datasets with those of the UN climate panel (IPCC)—which uses proxies like ice cores, tree rings, and coral—suggests that 2023 will be the hottest year in 125,000 years. Burgess noted that while September 2023’s record temperature was unexpected, such climate records are being broken increasingly often. Michael Mann, a climate scientist from the University of Pennsylvania, pointed out that El Nino years frequently set new records, as human-driven warming intensifies the natural effects of El Nino. This extreme warmth has already contributed to destructive weather events worldwide in 2023, including devastating floods in Libya, severe heatwaves across South America, and the worst wildfire season ever recorded in Canada. Piers Forster of the University of Leeds emphasized the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to prevent these disasters from becoming routine, suggesting that rapid action could halve the current pace of planetary warming. Although countries have announced more ambitious plans to cut emissions, global carbon dioxide levels reached a new record in 2022. Scientists caution that significant action is urgent, or else escalating climate extremes may soon become a regular occurrence.

Samantha Burgess, adjunct-directeur van C3S, omschreef de temperatuurpiek in oktober als ‘zeer extreem’. Zij wijt deze uitzonderlijke warmte aan voortdurende uitstoot van broeikasgassen door menselijk handelen en de komst van El Niño, een weerseffect dat het oppervlaktewater in de oostelijke Stille Oceaan verwarmt. Wereldwijd was de gemiddelde temperatuur aan het aardoppervlak in oktober 2023 1,7°C hoger dan in het pre-industriële tijdperk (1850-1900), aldus Copernicus. Authorities in Mijas, on Spain’s Costa del Sol, are investigating the possibility of a second crocodile on the loose after finding fresh footprints near the resort town of Mijas, close to Marbella. This follows the discovery earlier in the week of a dead crocodile, which had prompted concerns after multiple sightings of a large reptile in the area.

The newly discovered footprints do not match those of the seven-foot-long Nile crocodile found dead earlier, according to local officials. The gardener who first alerted authorities last month after spotting what was nicknamed the ‘Costa Croc’ maintains he saw a bigger animal than the one recovered.

The lakes where the dead crocodile was found, known as Majada Vieja, are located near the summer residences of actor Pierce Brosnan and singer Julio Iglesias, as well as holiday apartments popular with British tourists. Warning signs remain around the lakes, in Spanish, advising of the ‘Grave danger. Crocodile on the loose.’ The area, a common walking and jogging spot next to a busy golf club, is being closely monitored by officials who have also erected a watch tower over concerns the reptile could become more active as temperatures rise.

The dead animal, a Nile crocodile estimated to be about 15 years old, is believed to have died from a head injury after a fall. Authorities suspect it was abandoned by a previous owner. Police are reportedly still seeking the owner. Council officials are considering having the animal stuffed for educational display to tourists.

Despite warnings, many British expatriates and holidaymakers have ventured around the lakes in hopes of spotting the reptile. Rose Bell, restaurant manager at El Soto Golf Club, said that police had advised them of the danger, adding, ‘We thought it was a joke at first, but with the signs up, it’s clear they’re serious. Still, we plan to walk there most nights to see if we can spot it. I’ve heard crocodiles can run fast, so I’ll be sure to run faster if I see it. I suspect it might be a caiman.’

Richard Seamark, who manages the golf shop, commented that most British customers found the situation amusing, joking about the idea of ‘croc-burgers’ if the animal was caught, referencing previous local wildlife issues with wild boars.

The lake is one of three man-made lakes overlooked by apartments predominantly owned by British residents. The region has suffered damage from wildfires in recent summers. Mijas town hall spokesperson Mario Bravo stated that the crocodile is unlikely to pose a significant threat to humans unless provoked or threatened, but cautioned that danger could occur if someone accidentally encountered it in the undergrowth or attempted to capture it. Police continue daily patrols, especially as the weather gets warmer and the animal may become more active after winter.

With the onset of spring, authorities warn that a second crocodile may emerge from hibernation in the area.

De politie is nog altijd op zoek naar deze persoon. De gemeente overweegt het dier op te zetten om het aan toeristen te tonen.

Ondanks de waarschuwingen hebben veel Britse expats en toeristen het gebied rond de meren bezocht in de hoop het reptiel te zien. Rose Bell, restaurantmanager bij El Soto Golf Club, vertelt dat de politie haar over het gevaar heeft ingelicht. 'We dachten eerst dat het een grap was, maar met de borden zie je dat ze het menen. Toch zijn we van plan er na werktijd te wandelen om te kijken of we het dier zien. Ik heb gehoord dat krokodillen snel kunnen rennen; ik zorg ervoor dat ik nog sneller ren als ik er één zie. Ik denk trouwens dat het stiekem een kaaiman is.'

Richard Seamark, manager van de golfshop, merkt op dat de Britse klanten de situatie vooral grappig vinden en grappen over ‘croc-burgers’ maken als het dier wordt gevangen, verwijzend naar eerdere problemen met wilde zwijnen.

Het meer is een van drie kunstmatige meren, omgeven door appartementen die grotendeels in Brits bezit zijn. De omgeving is de afgelopen zomers getroffen door bosbranden. Volgens gemeentewoordvoerder Mario Bravo vormt de krokodil waarschijnlijk geen groot gevaar voor mensen, tenzij zij het dier bedreigen of proberen te vangen. Het risico zou echter toenemen als iemand per ongeluk op het dier stuit in het struikgewas. De politie patrouilleert dagelijks in het gebied, zeker nu het warmer wordt en het dier mogelijk actiever wordt na de winter.

Nu de lente begint, waarschuwen de autoriteiten dat een tweede krokodil uit zijn winterslaap tevoorschijn kan komen.

article_content:
Country music singer and sausage business founder Jimmy Dean passed away at his home in Varina, Virginia, on Sunday evening at the age of 81, according to police. Dean, a Country Music Hall of Fame member, was with his wife Donna at the time. Police spokesperson R.J. Clark stated that Dean appears to have died of natural causes.

Dean gained fame for his song "Big Bad John," which reached No. 1 on both the country and pop charts in 1961 and earned him a Grammy Award. His storytelling in songs produced other hits, including "Little Black Book" and "P.T. 109"—the latter inspired by John F. Kennedy's World War II experience.

Beginning in 1963, Dean hosted ABC's "The Jimmy Dean Show" for three years, with notable guests like Roger Miller and puppeteer Jim Henson, who introduced Rowlf the piano-playing dog. Dean also acted as Josh Clements in NBC’s "Daniel Boone" during the late 1960s.

Around the same period, Dean launched the Jimmy Dean Meat Company. He sold the company to Sara Lee Foods in 1984 but stayed on as chairman and spokesperson, maintaining a public presence for years.

Born Seth Ward in Olton, Texas, on August 10, 1928, Dean learned to play piano from his mother at age ten and later picked up guitar, harmonica, and accordion. After his 1948 discharge from the Air Force, he formed the Texas Wildcats band and performed in the Washington, D.C., area. Dean is quoted as saying, “We played every dive in Washington at one time or another. And dives is what they were,” according to the Country Music Hall of Fame’s biography.

Dean was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame this year. Reporting contributed by CNN’s Leslie Tripp.

Clark verklaarde dat Dean vermoedelijk aan natuurlijke oorzaken is overleden.

Dean verwierf bekendheid met het nummer "Big Bad John", dat in 1961 de eerste plaats bereikte in zowel de country- als de poplijsten en hem een Grammy Award opleverde. article_content: Earlier this year, in the Believer Meats test kitchen, Chef Andres Voloschin prepared chicken strips produced from cultivated cells rather than traditional poultry. More than 150 startups worldwide—including Believer Meats—are striving to create meat that doesn't require raising or slaughtering animals. Their aim is to deliver affordable, tasty alternatives that closely resemble conventional meat, while reducing environmental impact and transforming global protein production—much like how electric cars are disrupting the automotive industry. Yaakov Nahmias, founder of Believer Meats, observes, "We are addicted to meat as a species. It's part of our evolution, our culture. But we've focused on quantity, not on the environment or sustainability." Israel, California, and Singapore have become prominent hubs for cultivated meat innovation. Companies in this emerging field, producing what is sometimes called cultivated, cultured, or lab-grown meat, are scaling up by forming partnerships with mainstream meat producers, attracting investment, and constructing new facilities—particularly in the United States. Despite this progress, widespread adoption of cell-based meat remains uncertain. Production is still expensive, scientific challenges exist (such as recreating the structure of steak), and government regulation poses hurdles. At present, only Singapore and the U.S. have approved cultivated meat for sale. While some consumers who have tried it report positive experiences, others remain wary. An AP-NORC poll found half of U.S. adults are unlikely to try it, often because 'it just sounds weird.' The technology borrows from advances in medical science. It begins with obtaining a sample of animal cells, which can originate from tissue, a fertilized egg, or a cell bank. Scientists select cells capable of self-renewal and differentiation into muscle and fat, using them to create cell lines that reduce the need for further animal sourcing. The cells are grown in bioreactors, nourished with a nutrient-rich broth, and, when producing structured products, are supported by scaffolds that shape their development. Proponents believe cultivated meat could dramatically reduce land use and resource consumption associated with conventional livestock farming. Glenn Gaudette, a biomedical engineering specialist at Boston College, highlighted the field's potential to mitigate environmental damage from animal agriculture. Nonetheless, reaching full equivalence with traditional meat will require more time and research, particularly regarding taste and texture for whole-cut products. Technical obstacles include finding optimal scaffolds and ensuring adequate oxygen delivery to all cells—solutions range from animal-based gelatin to plant-based structures like decellularized spinach. Experts are confident technical problems will eventually be solved, but shifting public attitudes is considered an even bigger challenge. For many, meat is closely linked to farming rather than laboratory production. In the AP-NORC poll, younger people (under 45) and men were more open to cultivated meat, but only 18% of all U.S. adults said they were very or extremely likely to try it. Safety is another significant concern. For example, Nora Bailey, a 31-year-old mother in rural Arkansas, voiced hesitation due to uncertainty about long-term health effects. The World Health Organization has outlined possible risks—including microbial contamination and potential allergens—while acknowledging conventional meat also carries food safety hazards. Since gaining regulatory approval in the U.S. and Singapore, a handful of restaurants and events have begun serving cultivated chicken. Early tasters, such as Karen Hunt, have responded positively, noting the familiar taste and texture. In summary, cultivated meat offers environmental and animal welfare benefits, but it faces substantial technical, regulatory, and cultural hurdles before it can become a viable replacement for conventional meat.
translated_content: Eerder dit jaar bereidde chef-kok Andres Voloschin in de testkeuken van Believer Meats kipreepjes, gemaakt van gekweekte cellen in plaats van van traditionele kip. Wereldwijd werken meer dan 150 startups—including Believer Meats—aan vlees dat geen dieren meer behoeft om te worden grootgebracht of geslacht. Ze willen betaalbare, smaakvolle alternatieven bieden die sterk lijken op conventioneel vlees, en tegelijkertijd de impact op het milieu verminderen en de wereldwijde eiwitproductie veranderen—net zoals elektrische auto's de auto-industrie veranderen. Yaakov Nahmias, oprichter van Believer Meats, zegt: "We zijn als soort verslaafd aan vlees. Het is deel van onze evolutie, onze cultuur. Maar we focusten op kwantiteit, niet op het milieu of duurzaamheid." Israël, Californië en Singapore zijn belangrijke centra voor innovatie in gekweekt vlees. Bedrijven in deze opkomende sector—ook wel gekweekt, gecultiveerd of laboratoriumvlees genoemd—schalen hun productie op door samen te werken met traditionele vleesproducenten, investeringen aan te trekken en nieuwe faciliteiten te bouwen, vooral in de Verenigde Staten. Toch blijft brede acceptatie van kweekvlees onzeker. De productie is nog duur, wetenschappelijke uitdagingen blijven bestaan (zoals het nabootsen van de textuur van biefstuk), en regelgeving is een obstakel. Op dit moment is de verkoop van kweekvlees alleen toegestaan in Singapore en de VS. Sommigen die het hebben geprobeerd zijn positief, anderen zijn sceptisch. Uit een AP-NORC-enquête blijkt dat de helft van de Amerikaanse volwassenen het waarschijnlijk niet zou proberen, vaak omdat het 'vreemd klinkt.' De technologie is gedeeltelijk afkomstig uit de medische wetenschap en begint met een monster van dierlijke cellen, afkomstig van weefsel, een bevrucht ei of een celbank. Wetenschappers selecteren cellen die kunnen vernieuwen en uitgroeien tot spier- en vetcellen, en maken zo celijnen zodat dieren minder vaak nodig zijn. De cellen groeien in bioreactoren met een voedzaam medium en, bij gestructureerde producten, op steigers die hun ontwikkeling sturen. Voorstanders geloven dat kweekvlees het gebruik van land en middelen voor traditionele veeteelt sterk kan verminderen. Glenn Gaudette, biomedisch ingenieur aan Boston College, benadrukt de potentiële positieve impact op het milieu. Toch duurt het nog jaren voordat deze producten gelijkwaardig zijn aan traditioneel vlees, met name qua smaak en textuur van hele stukken. Technische uitdagingen zijn onder andere het vinden van geschikte steigers en voldoende zuurstofvoorziening—oplossingen variëren van gelatine tot plantstructuren zoals ontcelde spinazie. Volgens experts kunnen de technische barrières worden overwonnen, maar het veranderen van de publieke houding is moeilijker. Veel mensen associëren vlees nog steeds met boerderijen in plaats van laboratoria. Uit de AP-NORC-enquête blijkt dat vooral jongvolwassenen (onder 45) en mannen iets enthousiaster zijn, maar slechts 18% van alle Amerikanen geeft aan het waarschijnlijk te willen proberen. Veiligheid is een belangrijk punt. Zo uitte Nora Bailey, een 31-jarige moeder uit landelijk Arkansas, haar zorgen over onbekende langetermijneffecten. De Wereldgezondheidsorganisatie benoemt mogelijke risico's zoals microbiële besmetting en allergieën, al kent conventioneel vlees ook voedselveiligheidsrisico's. Na goedkeuring in de VS en Singapore bieden enkele restaurants en evenementen nu kweekkip aan. De eerste proevers reageren meestal positief; Karen Hunt roemde bijvoorbeeld de vertrouwde smaak en textuur. Kortom: kweekvlees biedt voordelen voor het milieu en dierenwelzijn, maar staat nog voor aanzienlijke technische, regelgevende en culturele uitdagingen voordat het traditioneel vlees echt kan vervangen.

One of the biggest barriers for women climbing the career ladder is the leap from entry-level to management, often called the 'broken rung.' The latest 'Women in the Workplace' report—produced by McKinsey & Company and Lean In—shows that women continue to face slower advancement at this early step. Examining 2022 data from 276 organizations and more than 10 million workers, the report found that only 87 women are promoted to manager for every 100 men.

Alexis Krivkovich, McKinsey senior partner, stressed that while much attention goes to the 'glass ceiling,' true progress relies on fixing the broken rung, which remains the most unequal stage. Lean In CEO Rachel Thomas echoed this, saying that until early promotions become more equitable, increases in women leaders further up are only short-term fixes.

According to the study, men hold 60% of first-level manager roles, compared to 40% for women. The imbalance widens at higher levels: women fill just 36% of senior manager/director and 28% of C-suite posts. For women of color, the gaps are even starker.

Krivkovich and Thomas pointed to several solutions: employers should address potential bias before promotion decisions, track promotions by gender and race, and require managers to explain their choices. Thomas highlighted research showing that explaining rationales decreases bias, and called for focused programs—like mentorship and sponsorship—for women of color to tackle the distinct hurdles they encounter.

Alexis Krivkovich, senior partner bij McKinsey, benadrukte dat hoewel veel aandacht wordt besteed aan het 'glazen plafond', echte vooruitgang afhangt van het repareren van de gebroken trede, die het meest ongelijk blijft. Voor vrouwen van kleur zijn de verschillen zelfs nog groter.

Krivkovich en Thomas noemen verschillende oplossingen: werkgevers zouden vooroordelen voor promotiebeslissingen moeten benoemen, promoties naar geslacht en etniciteit moeten monitoren en leidinggevenden moeten vragen hun keuzes toe te lichten. Ze pleit ook voor gerichte mentor- en sponsorprogramma’s voor vrouwen van kleur om hun specifieke obstakels op het werk aan te pakken.

article_content: A Japanese sushi chain, Sushiro, is replacing its traditional revolving sushi conveyor belts with touchscreens at three of its stores, following a series of hygiene-related pranks by customers who filmed themselves tampering with food. These pranks, dubbed 'sushi terrorism,' were inspired by viral social media videos and included acts like licking shared soy sauce bottles and touching sushi as it passed by on the conveyor. As a result, Sushiro will now use animated displays on touchscreens at each table to simulate the 'kaiten' sushi experience. The company stated that these incidents have led to more than $100 million in claimed losses and a sharp decline in customers. Five people have been arrested in connection with the pranks, which have caused significant reputational damage to both Sushiro and the broader conveyor-belt sushi concept.

Deze grappen, 'sushi-terrorisme' genoemd, werden geïnspireerd door virale video's op sociale media en bestonden onder andere uit het likken van gedeelde sojasausflessen en het aanraken van sushi op de band. Hierdoor introduceert Sushiro nu geanimeerde displays op iedere tafel om de 'kaiten'-sushibeleving te simuleren. Het bedrijf gaf aan dat deze incidenten tot meer dan $100 miljoen aan schadeclaims en een sterke daling van het aantal klanten hebben geleid. Vijf mensen zijn gearresteerd in verband met de grappen, die aanzienlijke reputatieschade veroorzaakten voor zowel Sushiro als het bredere sushibandconcept.

article_content: Recent allegations that babies were decapitated in large numbers at a kibbutz in Israel during Hamas's terror attacks—claims repeated by U.S. President Biden and others—are now being reconsidered by both Israeli and White House officials. An Israeli official stated, 'There have been cases of Hamas militants carrying out beheadings and other ISIS-style atrocities. However, we cannot confirm if the victims were men or women, soldiers or civilians, adults or children.' A US administration official later clarified President Biden's remarks to CNN, noting that neither Biden nor his aides had seen images or received confirmed reports of children or infants being beheaded by Hamas. The official said Biden was referring to comments previously made by media outlets and Israeli officials. This echoes dynamics from the first Gulf War, where rumors outpaced confirmed facts. While it is true that infants were among those murdered, the specific 'baby massacre' claims remain unverified. The rapid spread and subsequent walk-back of these allegations have intensified public emotions without altering entrenched beliefs.

Een Israëlische functionaris verklaarde: 'Er zijn gevallen geweest waarbij Hamas-strijders onthoofdingen en andere ISIS-achtige wreedheden hebben uitgevoerd. Toch kunnen we niet bevestigen of de slachtoffers mannen of vrouwen, soldaten of burgers, volwassenen of kinderen waren.' Een Amerikaanse regeringsfunctionaris verduidelijkte later tegenover CNN de opmerkingen van president Biden en merkte op dat noch Biden noch zijn medewerkers beelden hebben gezien of bevestigde berichten hebben ontvangen over kinderen of baby's die door Hamas zouden zijn onthoofd. De functionaris zei dat Biden verwees naar eerder gemaakte opmerkingen van nieuwsmedia en Israëlische functionarissen. article_content: California will soon make it illegal for licensed therapists to attempt to change the sexual orientation of minors. Governor Jerry Brown signed the bill into law, which will take effect on January 1. The legislation, passed by the state Senate in May, prohibits attempts to alter the sexual orientation of patients under 18. Governor Brown stated, "This bill bans non-scientific 'therapies' that have driven young people to depression and suicide. These practices have no basis in science or medicine." Practitioners of so-called 'reparative therapy,' such as David Pickup of the National Association for Research and Therapy of Homosexuality, dispute the governor's statements. Pickup says his organization, along with some therapists and clients who are minors, plans to file a lawsuit challenging the law. The Pacific Justice Institute also announced it will file a separate lawsuit, alleging the law violates First Amendment rights. Pickup, who says he has both undergone and now administers such therapy, told CNN that the ban is a form of political and therapeutic irresponsibility and claims the therapy can help children resolve unwanted feelings of homosexuality. Pickup referenced a report by the American Psychiatric Association, stating it does not prove reparative therapy causes harm. However, the association, which represents over 36,000 members, has found that such therapy poses significant risks, including a greater likelihood of depression, anxiety, and self-destructive behaviors. The APA states that aligning therapy with anti-homosexual societal views may increase self-hatred in patients. The American Psychiatric Association says there is longstanding consensus in the behavioral and social sciences that homosexuality is a normal and positive variation of human sexual orientation. After the Senate vote, Rebekah Orr, spokeswoman for Equality California, described the bill as a vital protection for young people against harmful therapies based on junk science. Orr's group, the largest in California advocating for full equality for LGBT individuals, believes the law will prevent therapists from promoting the false idea that sexual orientation is a disorder. Peter Drake, who underwent conversion therapy, supports the bill, saying that this type of therapy is very harmful and ineffective. Pickup argues that children who come to him for therapy do so voluntarily and are seeking help due to distress. He claims that therapeutic intervention can address underlying causes, such as abuse or unmet emotional needs, which he believes contribute to homosexuality. He contends that when these issues are resolved, homosexual feelings diminish naturally, crediting therapy with reducing his own depression and increasing self-esteem. The upcoming lawsuits from Pickup's group and the Pacific Justice Institute, a legal network focused on constitutional rights, are expected to challenge the law, possibly by arguing about child abuse and the law’s constitutionality. Brad Dacus, president of the Pacific Justice Institute, criticized the bill strongly. Ryan Kendall, who experienced conversion therapy as a minor after being outed by his mother, said he was told his sexuality could be changed, but he never believed it. He described his identity as unchangeable and said the therapy caused him emotional harm. Kendall said psychologist Joseph Nicolosi treated him. His parents provided documentation from Nicolosi's office, but Nicolosi did not recall treating Kendall and maintained that his therapy is only for people who wish to change and is not harmful. George Rekers, another psychologist previously involved in reparative therapy, treated a boy named Kirk Murphy, whom he claimed stopped displaying feminine behavior. However, Murphy's family reported that he remained gay and later died by suicide. Rekers said it is inaccurate to conclude therapy caused the suicide, stating independent evaluations found improvement after treatment. Rekers’ reputation suffered after he hired a male escort for a European trip. He denied any sexual contact or knowledge of sexual services offered. Earlier in the year, psychiatrist Robert L. Spitzer retracted his 2003 study suggesting reparative therapy could change sexual orientation, admitting the study was flawed and apologizing to the gay community. Kendall says reparative therapy led to long periods of emotional distress, homelessness, and substance abuse, asserting that such therapy is baseless and harmful to children.
translated_content: Californië zal het binnenkort illegaal maken voor bevoegde therapeuten om te proberen de seksuele geaardheid van minderjarigen te veranderen. Gouverneur Jerry Brown heeft het wetsvoorstel ondertekend, dat op 1 januari van kracht wordt. De wet, die in mei door de Senaat werd aangenomen, verbiedt pogingen om de seksuele geaardheid van patiënten onder de 18 jaar te wijzigen. Gouverneur Brown verklaarde: "Deze wet verbiedt niet-wetenschappelijke ‘therapieën’ die jongeren tot depressie en zelfmoord hebben gedreven. Deze praktijken hebben geen basis in wetenschap of geneeskunde." Beoefenaars van de zogenaamde 'reparatieve therapie', zoals David Pickup van de National Association for Research and Therapy of Homosexuality, bestrijden de uitspraken van de gouverneur. Pickup zegt dat zijn organisatie, samen met enkele therapeuten en minderjarige cliënten, van plan is een rechtszaak aan te spannen tegen de wet. Het Pacific Justice Institute kondigde ook aan een aparte rechtszaak aan te spannen, waarin wordt beweerd dat de wet in strijd is met het Eerste Amendement. Pickup, die zegt dat hij zowel deze therapie heeft ondergaan als nu uitvoert, vertelde aan CNN dat het verbod een vorm van politieke en therapeutische onverantwoordelijkheid is en beweert dat de therapie kinderen kan helpen om ongewenste gevoelens van homoseksualiteit op te lossen. Pickup verwees naar een rapport van de American Psychiatric Association, waarin volgens hem niet wordt aangetoond dat reparatieve therapie schade veroorzaakt. De associatie, die meer dan 36.000 leden vertegenwoordigt, heeft echter vastgesteld dat dergelijke therapie aanzienlijke risico’s met zich meebrengt, waaronder een grotere kans op depressie, angst en zelfdestructief gedrag. De APA stelt dat het overeenstemmen met anti-homoseksuele opvattingen in therapie het zelfhaatgevoel bij patiënten kan versterken. Volgens de American Psychiatric Association is er binnen de gedrag- en sociale wetenschappen een lang bestaande consensus dat homoseksualiteit een normale en positieve variant is van menselijke seksuele geaardheid. Na de stemming in de Senaat omschreef Rebekah Orr, woordvoerster van Equality California, de wet als een essentiële bescherming voor jongeren tegen schadelijke therapieën op basis van pseudowetenschap. Haar organisatie, de grootste in Californië die staat voor volledige gelijkheid van LGBT-personen, gelooft dat de wet therapeuten zal beletten het valse idee te verspreiden dat seksuele geaardheid een stoornis is. Peter Drake, die conversietherapie onderging, steunt de wet en stelt dat deze vorm van therapie zeer schadelijk en ineffectief is. Pickup stelt dat kinderen die voor therapie bij hem komen dit vrijwillig doen en hulp zoeken vanwege hun problemen. Hij beweert dat therapeutische interventie onderliggende oorzaken kan aanpakken, zoals misbruik of onvervulde emotionele behoeften, die volgens hem bijdragen aan homoseksualiteit. Hij stelt dat wanneer deze problemen worden opgelost, homoseksuele gevoelens op natuurlijke wijze afnemen, en hij schrijft therapie toe aan het verminderen van zijn eigen depressie en het vergroten van zijn zelfvertrouwen. De aankomende rechtszaken van Pickup’s groep en het Pacific Justice Institute, een juridisch netwerk gefocust op grondwettelijke rechten, zullen de wet waarschijnlijk aanvechten, mogelijk met het argument dat het om kindermishandeling of ongrondwettigheid gaat. Brad Dacus, president van het Pacific Justice Institute, uitte scherpe kritiek op de wet. Ryan Kendall, die als minderjarige conversietherapie onderging nadat hij door zijn moeder werd geout, zei dat hem werd verteld dat zijn geaardheid veranderd kon worden, maar dat hij dat nooit geloofde. Hij beschreef zijn identiteit als onveranderlijk en zei dat de therapie hem emotionele schade heeft toegebracht. Kendall zei dat psycholoog Joseph Nicolosi hem heeft behandeld. Zijn ouders overhandigden documenten van Nicolosi’s praktijk, maar Nicolosi herinnerde zich niet dat hij Kendall heeft behandeld en stelde dat zijn therapie alleen bedoeld is voor mensen die zelf willen veranderen en niet schadelijk is. George Rekers, een andere psycholoog die eerder betrokken was bij reparatieve therapie, behandelde een jongen genaamd Kirk Murphy, waarvan hij beweerde dat deze na de therapie geen vrouwelijk gedrag meer vertoonde. Murphy’s familie gaf echter aan dat hij homoseksueel bleef en later door zelfmoord om het leven kwam. Rekers zei dat het niet juist is om aan te nemen dat de therapie tot de zelfmoord heeft geleid, en wees op beoordelingen van anderen die verbetering na de behandeling zagen. Rekers’ reputatie raakte beschadigd nadat hij een mannelijke escort meenam op een reis naar Europa. Hij ontkende enig seksueel contact of kennis van seksuele diensten. Eerder dit jaar trok psychiater Robert L. Spitzer zijn studie uit 2003 in, waarin werd gesuggereerd dat reparatieve therapie seksuele geaardheid zou kunnen veranderen. Hij gaf toe dat de studie gebrekkig was en bood zijn excuses aan aan de homogemeenschap. Kendall zegt dat reparatieve therapie voor lange periodes van emotionele problemen, dakloosheid en middelenmisbruik zorgde, en beweert dat deze therapieën ongegrond zijn en kinderen schaden.

article_content: When people want to give back to their community, they often reach for their checkbooks. Jayson Black, a 28-year-old IT consultant, chose instead to put on his running shoes. He pledged to run 26.2 miles daily for 26 days—a total of 681.2 miles—to raise money and awareness for the Three Square Food Bank of Southern Nevada. “My hope is that people will hear about this mission and become more aware,” Black said on the eighth day of his challenge. “Las Vegas isn’t just about bright lights and big hotels; in the areas around the Strip, many people are hungry.” Black’s effort came to CNN’s attention through Chris Morrow, a longtime iReporter in Las Vegas who read about the campaign. Black spent Thanksgiving Day on the streets: he woke up, attended church, then ran a marathon before returning home for a meal of salad and protein shakes. He explains he took on this challenge to highlight the ongoing issue of hunger in the community, beyond just holiday giving. “Every city in America has people going hungry. It’s about more than just Thanksgiving,” he says. According to Feeding America, about 16.2% of Southern Nevada’s population is 'food insecure', higher than the national average of 14.5% in 2012. Nationally, about 17.6 million households are considered food insecure. Matt Muldoon, chief development officer at Three Square Food Bank, attributes continued area poverty to the economic downturn of 2008—foreclosures, bankruptcies, and high unemployment. “Any recovery happening nationally isn’t fully reflected here,” Muldoon says. While Black had never officially competed in a marathon, he often ran similar distances, including once running 52 miles in a day. Muldoon trusted Black could complete the challenge. “Jay was very calm and confident about physically accomplishing this feat,” Muldoon said. Black began each day at 4:15 a.m., preparing with an energizing shake and a hot shower before running another 26.2 miles. He faced difficulties like finding open roads and even suffered a shin injury and stress fracture, but kept going. “I see my body as an engine. Unless doctors say to stop, I'm going to keep moving,” he said. His announcement of the plan met mixed responses from friends—some were doubtful but ultimately inspired once learning the reason behind his efforts. Whenever obstacles or pain caused him to doubt himself, seeing the impact on homeless people along his run motivated him further. “When I explained what I was doing, people would thank me. It’s rewarding to know we haven’t forgotten about those in need,” Black shared. Black’s campaign aimed to raise both money and nonperishable food for the food bank. While Muldoon did not focus on a specific fundraising target, Black’s initial goal was $4,000, and he ultimately raised $4,024, all of which will go to Three Square Food Bank. Each dollar provides about three meals due to the food bank’s efficiency. To honor his achievement, the Clark County Board of Commissioners declared December 23, 2013, Jayson Black Day. After finishing his challenge, Black expressed a sense of accomplishment. “I feel truly blessed,” he said, adding that his team would soon plan for the following year. Though his mission has ended, Black encourages others to contribute to their communities in their own way. “You don’t have to run 26 marathons to make a difference,” he says. “Anyone can help make someone smile.”

'Toen ik uitlegde wat ik deed, bedankten mensen me. Het is bijzonder om te weten dat we deze mensen niet zijn vergeten,' aldus Black. Black’s campagne richtte zich op het inzamelen van zowel geld als houdbare voedingsmiddelen voor de voedselbank. Hoewel Muldoon geen specifiek streefbedrag benadrukte, was Black’s oorspronkelijke doel $4.000, en uiteindelijk haalde hij $4.024 op—alles gaat naar de Three Square Food Bank. 'Ik voel me echt gezegend,' zei hij, eraan toevoegend dat zijn team snel plannen zal maken voor het volgende jaar. Hoewel zijn missie ten einde is, moedigt Black anderen aan om zich ook op hun eigen manier in te zetten voor hun gemeenschap. 'Je hoeft geen 26 marathons te lopen om het verschil te maken,' zegt hij. 'Iedereen kan iets doen om iemand te laten glimlachen.'

Comedian and activist Russell Brand faced tough questioning during a Channel 4 News interview about his campaign to reform drug laws and overhaul the political system. Brand, who argues parliamentary democracy is ineffective, aims to trigger a debate on drug laws in the House of Commons through a petition. However, anchor Jon Snow challenged Brand, suggesting the petition could support the very system Brand seeks to undermine.

Brand appeared frustrated as he defended his views, admitting his strategy might have some inconsistencies. He maintains that politicians are out of touch, and insists radical change is required, particularly in how society approaches drug addiction. Despite encouraging his supporters not to vote, Brand asserts his intention is to highlight flaws in the system, not reinforce them.

Brand’s high-profile stance has drawn mixed reactions, with some politicians and public figures criticizing him for using his celebrity status to disrupt the political landscape.

Employees from Philadelphia Gas Works were responding to a gas main break in the city's Tacony neighborhood when the explosion occurred, said fire department spokesman Jim Smith. "They were trying to control it and found a source of ignition," Smith explained. Among the injured were four PGW employees and a firefighter, with some of the injuries described as serious. CNN's Jason Kessler contributed to this report.

London’s East End, known for its notorious history, is also the birthplace of legendary director Alfred Hitchcock. Before rising to fame in Hollywood with classics like "Psycho" and "The Birds," Hitchcock was a major figure in British cinema, leaving his mark across London.

The British Film Institute recently restored nine of Hitchcock’s rarely viewed silent films, now screening in theaters after nearly 80 years. His ties to the city are commemorated in locations such as Leytonstone, where he was born in 1899 above his family’s shop. Although the original building is gone, a plaque marks the spot. Leytonstone Tube Station features mosaics celebrating his legacy, and a nearby pub bears his name.

Hitchcock frequently used London’s streets and landmarks in his movies. He achieved early recognition with “The Lodger” in 1927, which includes scenes from areas like Westminster and Charing Cross. Films such as 'Blackmail' staged suspenseful sequences at the British Museum, while his fascination with London’s dark side led him to seek inspiration from places like Scotland Yard’s 'Black Museum.'

Throughout his career, Hitchcock’s films showcased notable London sites: Covent Garden Market appears in 'Frenzy,' while 'Sabotage' features Trafalgar Square and London Zoo. Although some historical locations have since vanished, new tributes—such as a sculpture near the old Gainsborough Studios—honor his influence. Fans can join walking tours to visit spots from his films and learn more about his story.

Hitchcock’s British works, including "The Man Who Knew Too Much" and his final London-based film "Frenzy," continue to attract audiences. Events like BFI Southbank’s ‘Genius of Hitchcock’ festival revive interest in his early projects, and themed tours offer movie buffs a chance to explore the city through Hitchcock’s lens.

article_content: Supercomputing'23 in Denver was as much about artificial intelligence (AI) as it was about high-performance computing (HPC). Every exhibitor, from CPU and accelerator makers to networking and storage vendors, was showcasing their latest AI advances—even water cooling system providers and representatives from the U.S. Department of Energy and Department of Defense.  A major highlight was Nvidia’s low-key presence. The company skipped its usual large booth, as nearly every system vendor already featured H100-based servers. Nvidia’s key announcement was Europe’s first exaflop-level supercomputer at the Julich Supercomputing Centre in Germany. Called Jupiter, this system is expected to become the continent’s largest and possibly the fastest AI supercomputer globally, employing the new Grace Hopper 200 (GH200) chips with enhanced memory capacity and bandwidth. Jupiter is built on Eviden's BullSequana XH3000 liquid-cooled architecture, featuring a 'booster module' with almost 24,000 Nvidia GH200 Superchips interconnected by Nvidia’s Quantum-2 InfiniBand platform.  Jupiter also includes a 'Cluster Module' powered by new European ARM CPUs developed by SiPearl and supplied by ParTec from Germany. SiPearl’s Rhea CPU offers a high memory data rate of 0.5 bytes per flop, which is nearly five times greater than most GPUs, enabling notable efficiency for data-intensive applications. Once operational, Jupiter will be the largest supercomputer in Europe and among the largest AI supercomputers worldwide.  Nvidia announced at Microsoft Ignite the launch of AI Foundry Services on Azure, providing foundation models and an Enterprise AI software suite now available on Microsoft’s cloud. Companies like SAP, Amdocs, and Getty Images are among the first to build and deploy custom large language models (LLMs) using these tools. During Ignite, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on stage, highlighting the growing partnership.  Cerebras Systems continued to distinguish itself as one of the few AI hardware startups with hundreds of millions in revenue. CEO Andrew Feldman cited major clients, including the UAE’s G42, pharmaceutical firms, research institutes, and supercomputing centers worldwide.  Microsoft, HPE Cray, and other companies generated significant buzz around the upcoming AMD MI300 family, with public release news scheduled for December 6. Satya Nadella also pre-announced AMD MI300's availability on Azure. Meanwhile, Micron showcased its HBM3e memory, promoting higher bandwidth and capacity compared to rivals Samsung and SK Hynix.  Microsoft unveiled its own AI Accelerator, Maia, with a strong focus on large language model performance. The Maia 100 features 64 GB of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) along with substantial SRAM. Despite some skepticism about memory capacity for demanding models like OpenAI’s GPT-4, Microsoft appears confident in its LLM strategy.  The rise of LLMs put startups like Groq Inc. and SambaNova Systems in the spotlight. Both companies, now offering AI-as-a-service, attracted crowds at their booths. Groq demonstrated industry-leading inference performance for Llama 2 70B, using a demo with a live alpaca named Bunny onsite, and claimed a tenfold boost over Nvidia GPUs for GPT-3 tasks, showcasing highly competitive throughput.  NeuReality, an Israeli startup led by CEO Moshe Tanach, previewed new inference hardware intended to reduce infrastructure costs and improve performance. NeuReality pairs its custom SoC and software with a range of accelerators, such as AMD FPGAs and Qualcomm’s updated Cloud AI100, aiming for 90% cost savings for LLM inference. IBM’s AIU prototype is also supported.  Untether.ai presented its second-generation SpeedAI at-memory accelerator, claiming best-in-class efficiency and significant reductions in energy usage—a hot topic among data center vendors at the event.  Many system vendors—Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro, Boston Ltd, Penguin, and others—demonstrated new server designs, focusing on next-generation chips from AMD and Nvidia and innovative cooling solutions to manage increasing power densities.  Not all news was positive. The OpenAI board of directors, which suddenly ousted CEO Sam Altman (who now joins Microsoft), drew criticism within the industry. Reports cite widespread dissatisfaction among OpenAI employees, with hundreds calling for Altman’s and Greg Brockman's reinstatement to prevent staff departures and further disruption.  HPC Wire reported a violation of Supercomputing’s code of conduct due to inappropriate attire. The conference reiterated its commitment to a respectful and harassment-free environment and opted not to display the offensive content.  Since 1987, Supercomputing has grown from a modest gathering into a major event with over 14,000 attendees and exhibitors, reflecting the rapid transformation of HPC by big data and AI. The community looks forward to even bigger advances at next year’s conference in Atlanta.

Het AIU-prototype van IBM wordt ook ondersteund. Veel systeemleveranciers—Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro, Boston Ltd, Penguin en anderen—lieten hun nieuwe serverontwerpen zien, met nadruk op next-gen chips van AMD en Nvidia en innovatieve koelsystemen om de hogere vermogensdichtheden aan te kunnen.  Niet al het nieuws was positief. De board van OpenAI, die plotseling CEO Sam Altman (die nu naar Microsoft gaat) ontsloeg, kreeg veel kritiek uit de sector. Volgens berichten zijn veel OpenAI-medewerkers ontevreden; honderden vragen om de terugkeer van Altman en Greg Brockman om vertrek en verdere verstoringen te voorkomen.  HPC Wire meldde een schending van de gedragscode van Supercomputing wegens ongepaste kleding. De conferentie onderstreepte haar inzet voor een respectvolle en veilige omgeving en koos ervoor de aanstootgevende inhoud niet te tonen.  Sinds 1987 is Supercomputing uitgegroeid van een bescheiden bijeenkomst tot een groot evenement met meer dan 14.000 deelnemers en exposanten, een weerspiegeling van de snelle transformatie van HPC door big data en AI. De community kijkt uit naar meer vooruitgang op de conferentie van volgend jaar in Atlanta.

A team of experienced FBI agents in New York is leading the federal civil rights investigation into the death of Eric Garner. This follows a grand jury decision not to indict Officer Daniel Pantaleo, who was involved in the 2014 incident. On July 17, Garner, an unarmed Black man, died when Pantaleo applied a chokehold during an arrest for allegedly selling untaxed cigarettes—despite the NYPD’s ban on chokeholds. Video of the arrest shows Garner repeatedly telling officers, 'I can’t breathe,' as he was held on the ground.

The FBI’s investigators include specialists in public corruption and complex cases, and the review will consider actions by officers and emergency workers, NYPD training procedures, and findings from internal investigations. An agent who worked on the Abner Louima case is also involved. Federal prosecutors in Brooklyn are overseeing the inquiry.

According to the city’s medical examiner, Garner’s death was a homicide caused by neck and chest compression during physical restraint, with underlying health issues—such as asthma and heart disease—also contributing. Authorities are also determining if a chokehold was in fact used and have begun reviewing internal evidence and interviewing witnesses.

Pantaleo’s lawyer claims there was no intention to violate rights or any racial motive, describing the event as routine. The grand jury consisted of 14 white and 9 nonwhite members and required at least 12 votes to indict.

Garner’s death sparked widespread protests and drew renewed attention to the NYPD’s 'stop-and-frisk' policy, previously ruled unconstitutional for racial profiling. The case, occurring shortly before the fatal police shooting of Michael Brown in Missouri, became emblematic of tensions over policing practices and racial justice. Prior lawsuits had been filed against Pantaleo alleging civil rights violations; one was dismissed and another is ongoing.

Het onderzoek richt zich op het handelen van politie- en hulpverleners ter plekke, de training van NYPD-agenten, en de uitkomsten van eerdere interne onderzoeken. Federale aanklagers in Brooklyn houden toezicht op het proces.

Volgens de medisch onderzoeker was Garners dood een doodslag door samendrukking van nek en borst tijdens politiegeweld, waarbij onderliggende gezondheidsproblemen—zoals astma en hartklachten—ook meespeelden. Garners overlijden leidde tot grootschalige protesten en bracht het 'stop-and-frisk'-beleid van de NYPD opnieuw onder de aandacht; dat beleid werd al eerder als ongrondwettig en discriminerend bestempeld. Met de zaak—die vlak voor de dood van Michael Brown in Missouri plaatsvond—werden spanningen rond politieoptreden en ras opnieuw zichtbaar. article_content: On Thursday, the USS Carney—a U.S. Navy guided-missile destroyer in the northern Red Sea—intercepted and shot down multiple cruise missiles and drones launched by Iranian-backed Houthi forces in Yemen. Pentagon officials stated these projectiles were possibly heading toward Israel. This is the first recent instance of a U.S. Navy ship in the Middle East engaging missiles and drones not directly targeted at it, and the first U.S. military action taken to defend Israel in the current Israel-Hamas crisis. The incident happened Thursday evening local time. Pentagon spokesman Brig. Gen. Pat Ryder initially reported that the Carney had intercepted three cruise missiles and several drones. Later updates from U.S. officials counted four cruise missiles and 14 drones downed, revising the earlier numbers. Preliminary U.S. assessments indicate the Carney was not the intended target. Ryder emphasized that it is still unclear exactly what the missiles and drones were targeting, but they were launched from Yemen and heading north, potentially toward Israel. The Houthis, who are backed by Iran, control much of northern Yemen and have previously targeted Saudi Arabia; this attack seems to have been aimed elsewhere. Last week, Houthi leader Abdel-Malek al-Houthi warned that if the U.S. intervened directly in Gaza, his group would respond with drones, missiles, and other military actions, asserting there are ‘red lines’ regarding Gaza. The missiles and drones were detected moving north over the Red Sea and were intercepted using SM2 missiles from the USS Carney. U.S. officials stated all intercepts occurred over water—not land—and no U.S. personnel were harmed. In response to rising regional tensions after the Israel-Hamas war began, the United States has strengthened its military presence. The USS Carney is part of the Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group, which was deployed to the eastern Mediterranean to deter Iran and Hezbollah from joining the conflict. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin recently extended the Ford group’s deployment and ordered additional U.S. fighter aircraft to the region. The USS Dwight D. Eisenhower carrier strike group is also set to join the Ford group soon. A senior U.S. official said the Carney's actions demonstrate U.S. deterrence and resolve. The risk to U.S. personnel and interests in the region has risen, especially after a deadly hospital explosion in Gaza increased tensions. Recently, U.S. forces shot down drones approaching U.S. bases in Iraq and Syria. One U.S. contractor died of cardiac arrest during an incident at an Iraqi base, and indirect fire was reported at Al Asad airbase. Steve Ganyard, an ABC News contributor and former Pentagon official, suggested the U.S. may need to deploy more naval assets in the Red Sea if it commits to defending Israel from southern attacks. He voiced concern over potential Iranian reactions but noted there is no clear evidence Iran seeks direct conflict with the U.S. or Israel. The USS Carney had recently transited the Suez Canal into the Red Sea. Its swift interception highlights U.S. efforts to deter broader conflict and protect national interests, according to Defense Department statements.
translated_content: Op donderdag heeft de USS Carney—een Amerikaanse geleide-wapenvernietiger in het noorden van de Rode Zee—meerdere kruisraketten en drones onderschept en neergehaald die waren gelanceerd door door Iran gesteunde Houthi-troepen in Jemen. Volgens functionarissen van het Pentagon waren deze projectielen mogelijk op weg naar Israël. Dit is de eerste keer in recente jaren dat een Amerikaans marineschip in het Midden-Oosten raketten en drones heeft onderschept die niet direct op het schip zelf gericht waren. Ook is het de eerste Amerikaanse militaire actie ter verdediging van Israël in de huidige Israël-Hamas-crisis. Het incident vond plaats op donderdagavond lokale tijd. Pentagon-woordvoerder brigadegeneraal Pat Ryder meldde aanvankelijk dat de Carney drie kruisraketten en meerdere drones had onderschept. Latere updates van Amerikaanse functionarissen maakten melding van vier kruisraketten en veertien drones die waren neergehaald, waarmee de eerdere cijfers werden bijgesteld. Uit voorlopige Amerikaanse beoordelingen blijkt dat de Carney niet het beoogde doelwit was. Ryder benadrukte dat het nog onduidelijk is waar de raketten en drones precies op waren gericht, maar ze waren gelanceerd vanuit Jemen en bewogen zich noordwaarts, mogelijk richting Israël. De Houthi's, die worden gesteund door Iran, controleren een groot deel van Noord-Jemen en hebben eerder met name Saudi-Arabië aangevallen; deze aanval leek echter op een ander gebied gericht. Vorige week waarschuwde Houthi-leider Abdel-Malek al-Houthi dat als de VS direct in Gaza zou ingrijpen, zijn groep zou reageren met drones, raketten en andere militaire acties, waarbij hij stelde dat er 'rode lijnen' zijn wat betreft Gaza. De raketten en drones werden waargenomen terwijl ze noordwaarts boven de Rode Zee trokken en werden met SM2-raketten vanaf de USS Carney uit de lucht gehaald. Amerikaanse functionarissen benadrukten dat alle onderscheppingen boven water plaatsvonden, niet boven land, en dat er geen Amerikaanse militairen gewond zijn geraakt. Naar aanleiding van de stijgende spanningen in de regio sinds het begin van de Israël-Hamas-oorlog, heeft de VS haar militaire aanwezigheid versterkt. De USS Carney maakt deel uit van het Gerald R. Ford luchtvaartcarrier-strike group, dat naar de oostelijke Middellandse Zee is gestuurd om Iran en Hezbollah te ontmoedigen zich bij het conflict aan te sluiten. Defensiesecretaris Lloyd Austin heeft onlangs de inzet van de Ford-groep verlengd en extra Amerikaanse gevechtsvliegtuigen naar de regio gestuurd. De USS Dwight D. Eisenhower carrier-strike group zal zich binnenkort bij de Ford-groep voegen. Een hoge Amerikaanse functionaris zei dat de actie van de Carney het afschrikkingsvermogen en de vastberadenheid van de VS laat zien. Het risico voor Amerikaans personeel en belangen in de regio is toegenomen, vooral na een dodelijke explosie in een ziekenhuis in Gaza die de spanningen verhoogde. Onlangs hebben Amerikaanse troepen drones neergehaald die Amerikaanse bases in Irak en Syrië naderden. Een Amerikaanse aannemer overleed aan een hartstilstand tijdens een incident op een basis in Irak en er werd indirect vuur gerapporteerd op luchtmachtbasis Al Asad. Steve Ganyard, een ABC News-medewerker en voormalig Pentagon-functionaris, suggereerde dat de VS mogelijk meer marineschepen in de Rode Zee moet inzetten als het zich blijft inzetten om Israël te beschermen tegen aanvallen uit het zuiden. Hij uitte zorg over mogelijke Iraanse reacties, maar merkte op dat er momenteel geen duidelijk bewijs is dat Iran direct conflict met de VS of Israël zoekt. De USS Carney was recent door het Suezkanaal de Rode Zee binnengevaren. De snelle onderschepping onderstreept volgens verklaringen van het Amerikaanse ministerie van Defensie de Amerikaanse inspanningen om bredere conflicten te voorkomen en nationale belangen te beschermen.
